audits.area: Reliability of the phone-to-glasses push and HUD self-update
audits.summary: The push path works when everything lines up, but nothing in it is confirmed from end to end. The phone shows "Playing on your glasses" as soon as the server accepts the push. The HUD acks (and the server deletes) the push before it decides whether to play it. Several confirmed paths make a push go nowhere without anyone seeing it: a single default-focused pinch on "New code" orphans the phone; pushes older than 10 minutes are consumed and skipped with nothing on screen; any "expired"-sounding error wipes the durable link; and the HUD's own keepalive marks the pair "Phone connected" with no phone at all (checked against production). There is also no self-update, and the build stamp has been frozen at "v1.25" since 2026-09-14, so even Diagnostics cannot show which code the glasses are running. The biggest opportunity is one closed loop on the existing /api/pair endpoint: the poll returns a build id (safe-moment reload), the HUD posts got/playing/pinch/failed/missed states, and the server records when the glasses last polled, so the phone can say what actually happened. Audit side effects: I created two throwaway pairs on production (E7AXH8, 453LPD) to check ack and touch behaviour, the same way scripts/selftest.mjs does. The harness also forwards /api/diag to production, so about 16 diag lines with origin 127.0.0.1 now appear in the Vercel logs.

findings.title: No self-update, and the build stamp is frozen, so fixes never reach the glasses and nobody can tell
findings.evidence: No visibilitychange, pageshow or reload logic exists in app.js or player.js (grep). index.html:70 still has window.GLASSTUBE_BUILD = '1.25', last changed in e915109 (2026-09-14), but app.js shipped again on 2026-10-08 (a379028, ?v=36). Diagnostics shows 'App: v1.25' for both builds (unpaired2-diag-additive.png). Caching is already right: on production, / returns cache-control no-store, and app.js?v=36 returns 'public, max-age=0, must-revalidate' with an etag. A reload is all it takes to get new code; nothing ever triggers one.
findings.recommendation: 1) Add scripts/stamp.mjs and run it before every `vercel --prod`. It hashes index.html, app.js, player.js, styles.css, prefs.js, sound.js and embed.html (8 hex chars), writes the hash into index.html (GLASSTUBE_BUILD and every ?v=) and writes api/_build.json. api/pair.js falls back to process.env.VERCEL_DEPLOYMENT_ID. 2) Every GET /api/pair response includes `build`. When d.build differs from GLASSTUBE_BUILD, the HUD sets updatePending and sends hudNote('update-pending') once. 3) Reload only at safe moments: (a) visibilitychange to visible, or pageshow, while current !== 'player' (the 'I reopened the app' moment, before the first input); (b) on home, list, settings, debug or phone with no key press for 20s; (c) on the player only when the video ended with nothing next, after 5 or more minutes paused, or once Left has landed on a menu (then rule b applies). Never reload mid-video or with search text typed. If a push arrives while an update is pending, play it on the old code first, because a reload resets user activation and the push would hit the 'Enter to play' gate. 4) Before reloading, call progressSave() and store {screen, focus index} in sessionStorage. Then call location.replace('/?b=' + build); a new URL defeats any in-memory copy. After load, restore the screen, show 'Updated' for 2s and send hudNote('updated', {from, to}). 5) Loop guard: store localStorage glasstube.updatedTo = {build, at} and allow at most one reload per build per 10 minutes. After that, Diagnostics shows 'Update waiting' instead of reloading again. 6) Bootstrap: the build now in memory has no updater, so one manual full close and reopen on the glasses is unavoidable. Old builds poll without &b=, so the server can tell the phone 'Your glasses are running an old GlassTube. Close it on the glasses and open it again.'

findings.title: The phone says 'Playing on your glasses' without confirmation, and the HUD acks (consumes) a push before deciding to play it
findings.evidence: Store.swift:528-529 sets 'Playing on your glasses.' when the server accepts the push and hasFile is true. app.js:1560-1574 posts the ack before the stale check and before applyPush or any route runs. Production probe on a throwaway pair: after ack seq 1 the next poll returns dest:null; ack 1 against a pending seq 2 leaves it intact. So an ack consumes the push, and no state about it is kept. Harness push with the HUD clock +20 min: [hud-report] {"ev":"push","stale":true,"ageS":1200}, and the HUD stayed on Home (skew-after-push-additive.png). The phone in that case would already say 'Playing'.
findings.recommendation: Keep it on /api/pair (Hobby allows 12 functions). Add columns to glasstube_pairs: ack_seq, ack_state, ack_detail, ack_at, hud_seen_at, hud_build, hud_visible, phone_seen_at. The HUD posts {code, ack: seq, state} at each step: 'got' on receipt (replaces today's ack), 'pinch' when the play gate shows, 'playing' on the first 'playing' event of that push's first video, 'failed' with the blockedText() sentence, and 'missed' for a stale push. The push response adds glassesSeenS, glassesBuild and glassesVisible. The phone then polls GET /api/pair?code=<key>&seq=<n> every 1s for up to 20s and rewrites the outcome text: 'Sending to your glasses...' → if glassesSeenS > 15: 'Sent, but your glasses haven't checked in for 4 min. Open GlassTube on the glasses.' → got: 'Your glasses got it...' → playing: 'Playing on your glasses.' → pinch: 'On your glasses: pinch to start.' → failed: 'The glasses couldn't play it: <detail>' → missed: 'Waiting on the glasses' home screen.' → no ack after 8s: 'Not picked up yet. Is GlassTube open on the glasses?' Never show 'Playing' before state=playing.

findings.title: 'New code' has focus by default on From iPhone, so one pinch silently orphans the phone
findings.evidence: Harness: opening From iPhone gives document.activeElement = 'btn-pair-new / New code' (red focus ring in paired2-phone-additive.png). Pinch runs app.js:1793-1800, which deletes both the code and the durable link and mints a new row. The old row stays valid for 365 days (HANDOFF.md:74-80). Store.reconnect (Store.swift:366-388) only unpairs on 'expired' or 'not active', so the phone keeps touching and pushing to a row nobody polls and still says 'Playing on your glasses'. This fits the live 'glasses polling a different pairing' theory. From iPhone is exactly where a user goes when nothing plays, and pinch is the natural action there.
findings.recommendation: index.html:187-190: make Back (or a non-destructive row) the first focusable. Rename 'New code' to 'Link a different phone', put it last, and require a second pinch within 4s ('Pinch again to unlink your iPhone'). Server: the HUD sends POST /api/pair {replaces: <old token>} when it mints a code. The server marks the old row superseded, and from then on touch or push on that row returns {ok:false, moved:true, error:'Your glasses were linked to a new code'}. The phone unpairs and asks for the new code instead of pushing into the void.

findings.title: The HUD's own keepalive touch marks the pair 'paired', so the glasses say 'Phone connected' with no phone
findings.evidence: Production probe: on a freshly minted pair, the poll returned paired:false. After POST {code:<token>, touch:true}, which is exactly what app.js:1544-1550 sends every 8th poll, the poll returned paired:true. The harness counted 2 HUD touches in about 34s. So about 16s after any new code, From iPhone shows 'Phone connected. Send a video from the iPhone app.' (app.js:1552-1554), and Diagnostics shows 'Phone pairing: paired' in green, even if no phone ever typed the code. The phone also shows 'Paired' just because it holds a link (Store.swift:107), without checking that any glasses poll it.
findings.recommendation: Separate claiming from keepalive. Drop the HUD touch (the poll should refresh last_activity on the server), or send it as {who:'hud'} so it never sets claimed. Only a phone touch or push sets claimed=true and phone_seen_at. The poll returns paired (claimed only) and phoneSeenS, and all glasses copy is driven by phoneSeenS (see the pairing-state finding).

findings.title: Stale pushes are still consumed and dropped with nothing on screen; judgeFresh review
findings.evidence: judgeFresh (api/pair.js:25-33) is correct for what it aims at: the server's clock wrote ts, so the server's clock judges it. The copy with Object.assign is safe, channels and session pushes are unaffected, and production poll2 came back without ts, so it is deployed. Gaps: (a) for pushes of 10 minutes or more, ts is kept and app.js:1569-1574 still compares it to the glasses' clock. A clock running more than 10 minutes behind replays old pushes when the app opens; a clock running ahead drops them. (b) Deleting ts blinds diagnostics: hudNote ageS is now always null. (c) A stale push is the common case ('I sent it while the glasses were asleep or the app was closed'), and it is acked, then skipped. The harness run with the clock +20 min shows exactly that: Home unchanged, no message (skew-after-push-additive.png).
findings.recommendation: Let the server decide in both directions. For a stale push set dest.ts = 1 (not 0: `dest.ts &&` treats 0 as fresh and would play it), so every legacy HUD drops it the same way. Add dest.ageS and dest.stale for new builds. A new HUD never compares clocks. For a stale push it acks with state 'missed' and puts a focusable card at the top of Home: 'Missed from iPhone · <title> · 14 min ago' (pinch plays it). Keep the last 3 in localStorage so a reload doesn't lose them.

findings.title: Any 'expired / not found / unknown' error wipes the durable link on the glasses and the phone
findings.evidence: app.js:1518-1531 deletes LINK_KEY and mints a new pair whenever d.error matches /expir|not active|not found|unknown/. On production, any key it can't find (a made-up 64-hex token or a made-up code) returns 'That code expired. Open From iPhone on the glasses for a new one.' The phone also unpairs on 'expired' (Store.swift:379). The uncommitted api/_rpc.js switches to api.atberth.com/rpc/ when the URL env points at Berth. If GLASSTUBE_SUPABASE_URL is flipped before glasstube_pairs (with link_token) is copied, or Berth returns any 'not found' or 'unknown' text, every pair of glasses and every phone unpairs on its next poll. Also, pairLastSeq is reset only by New code (app.js:1796), and a new row's first push is destSeq 1 (production probe). If the old pair's last seq was also 1, the first push to the new pair is neither played nor acked until a reload.
findings.recommendation: The server returns a structured {ok:false, gone:true} only when the row is really missing or expired. The HUD wipes its link only after 3 gone responses in a row spread over at least 30s, and never because the 6-character code expired while a link exists. Reset pairLastSeq whenever the key changes, persist it per key, and accept a dest only when destSeq > lastSeq. The phone handles 'gone' the same way. Copy the pair rows before flipping the env var.

findings.title: One failed poll during playback leaves a red 'No internet. Retrying...' bar on the player for good
findings.evidence: Harness: during playback, one /api/pair fetch was rejected at 24.17s. The status became 'No internet. Retrying...' (status-err) at 24.63s and was still showing 8s later, after polls had succeeded again (blip2-after-blip-additive.png). Cause: app.js:326-330, where setOffline(false) clears the bar only when !nowPlaying. The pollPair catch (app.js:1577-1580) also calls setOffline(true) for any failure, including a non-JSON 5xx, which is a server problem, not 'no internet'.
findings.recommendation: setOffline(false) clears #status whenever the text showing is the offline text, playing or not. Declare offline only after 2 failures in a row (about 4s) or when navigator.onLine === false. Say 'Can't reach GlassTube' for HTTP or parse errors. On the player, use a small dim corner badge instead of a full-width red bar over the video.

findings.title: Push receipt is almost invisible on the glasses: no 'Got it from your iPhone'
findings.evidence: A status trace after a push showed [[4156,'Playing from your phone.'],[6538,'']]. The only receipt cue is a 14px #c9c9c9 line at the bottom (app.js:976-978), and show() wipes it (app.js:255) on the first route retry. In a second run it was gone before paint. The load gate says only 'Loading...' (push-before.png), and the play gate says only 'Enter to play' (push-t13.png). Nothing tells the wearer the phone sent this.
findings.recommendation: Add a dedicated #toast that setStatus() and show() don't touch. On receipt, show a pill at the top for 3s, 20-22px white text on black with a 1px #555 border (no large bright fill on an additive display): 'From your iPhone · <title>'. It must survive route retries. Set the load-gate msg to 'From your iPhone · starting...'. For a pushed video, the play gate reads 'Pinch to play' with the sub-line 'Sent from your iPhone' (say 'Pinch', not 'Enter', on the glasses). Channels and session pushes use the same toast ('Channels updated from your iPhone').

findings.title: Pairing state isn't readable: always 'listening', setup steps shown after linking, no last-push or freshness
findings.evidence: The Home subtitle is always 'Code TESTQA · listening' (app.js:493-498), even while polls fail or after the code expired. When already linked, From iPhone still shows '1. Open GlassTube on your iPhone 2. Type this code 3. Paste a YouTube link' (paired2-phone-additive.png). Nowhere shows when the last push arrived or what happened to it. The first screen of Diagnostics is App v1.25, Origin, Viewport, Online, pairing and link, then a textarea, with no last-poll age, last push, phone-seen time or real build (unpaired2-diag-additive.png).
findings.recommendation: Home subtitle states: 'iPhone linked · seen 2 min ago', 'iPhone linked · not seen since yesterday', 'Waiting for iPhone · code ABC123', 'Can't reach GlassTube · retrying'. From iPhone when linked: headline 'Linked to your iPhone', a small line 'Code ABC123 · the same code shows in the iPhone app's Glasses tab', and 'Last from iPhone: <title> · 3 min ago · played'; hide the steps. Diagnostics, first rows: Build (hash), Server build / Update pending, Pair key (code + last 4 of token), Last poll (Xs ago, ok or error), Poll every (s), Phone seen, Last push (seq · age · got/playing/pinch/failed/missed).

findings.title: Fixed 2s poll in every state, with no timeout or overlap guard; make it adaptive
findings.evidence: app.js:23 and 1483-1488 use setInterval(pollPair, 2000) on every screen, when hidden and during playback. The harness counted 17 GET and 2 touch POSTs in about 34s, which is about 2,000 function invocations plus DB RPCs per hour per pair of glasses. Each one wakes WiFi on a small battery, and 4h a day comes to about 240k invocations a month, a large share of the Hobby plan's monthly allowance. There is no AbortController or in-flight guard, so on slow WiFi polls pile up. Because app.js:1560 tests destSeq !== lastSeq rather than >, an older response arriving late can re-apply an earlier push over a newer one.
findings.recommendation: Use a setTimeout chain with one request in flight and an 8s AbortController timeout. Schedule: hidden: stop. Visible, and on From iPhone, or a key pressed in the last 60s, or the server says the phone was active in the last 2 min: 2s. Menus idle: 6s. Idle more than 10 min: 15s. Playing: 10s. Errors: back off 2/4/8/15s. Poll immediately on visibilitychange to visible, pageshow, focus and online. The server returns nextPollMs, so the policy can change without a HUD deploy, and the phone's foreground touch speeds the glasses up while someone is choosing a video. Drop the HUD touch (the poll refreshes activity), or send it every 30 minutes. Accept a dest only when destSeq > lastSeq. Expect about 300-500 requests an hour while watching, and push latency of 2s or less while the phone is in use.

findings.title: Hidden or background HUD instances keep polling and can consume a push nobody sees
findings.evidence: There is no visibilitychange or pagehide handling anywhere in app.js or player.js (grep). The glasses keep the page alive for days, and an ack consumes the dest (production probe), so whichever instance polls first wins. A hidden instance would ack and 'play' a push the wearer never sees, while the phone says Playing. hudNote 'push' already includes vis, so a hidden consume would appear as "vis":"hidden" in the logs.
findings.recommendation: Stop polling while document.hidden. If a dest is somehow received while hidden, don't ack it. Add a random per-instance id to the poll query, so the server logs, and through the status API the phone, can see two pollers on one key.

findings.title: The relay escape hatch can strand the glasses app on the phone's HTTP page
findings.evidence: openRelay calls location.replace to http://<phone LAN>/p/<id> (app.js:989-997). The relay page (MediaRelay.swift:255-280) has no keydown handler and only goes back to the HUD after 'ended' or 2 errors. If the wearer pauses or leaves mid-video, the glasses' GlassTube app stays on that page, which is kept in memory for days. From then on there is no polling and no self-update, and pushes never land while the phone says Playing.
findings.recommendation: On the relay page, ArrowLeft or Escape calls back(), and so does visibilitychange to visible while the video is paused. Show a small 'Left · back to GlassTube' hint. Make back() go to '/?from=relay' so the HUD can say 'Back from phone playback'.

findings.title: Server logs can't show which device polls which pair, and the durable token travels in URLs
findings.evidence: api/pair.js:8-18 logs one poller line per 30s per function instance across all keys, so a second key is invisible. hudNote doesn't carry UA, build or instance. The poll puts the 64-hex link token in the query string (app.js:1514), so it ends up in request logs. Vercel kept only about the last hour of logs: today only my own probe calls were visible, so evidence of the live bug is gone before anyone looks.
findings.recommendation: Rate-limit the log per key (a Map of key to last-logged time) and include build, instance and visibility. Persist hud_seen_at, hud_build and hud_visible in the pair row; that also feeds the confirmation loop. Send the key in a header or POST body instead of the URL.

findings.title: Uncommitted account sync can bring back a dead pairing on a phone
findings.evidence: Store.swift:327-337 (uncommitted) copies the account's pairing link onto any phone that has none. Superseded rows stay valid (see the 'New code' finding), so after a reinstall, or on a second phone, the app adopts the old row, reconnect() succeeds, the phone shows Paired and pushes go nowhere.
findings.recommendation: Adopt the account's link only if the touch response shows the glasses polled that row within the last day (hudSeenS) and the row isn't superseded. Otherwise show 'Type the code shown on your glasses'.

audits.area: Navigation and interaction with the Neural Band (arrows + pinch, Left = back)
audits.summary: The basic model works: Up/Down move a single focus, pinch selects, Left goes back in lists, and Continue resumes in one pinch. Five things break it, all confirmed in the harness. Back always resets focus to the first row. A pinch on the default-focused button unlinks the phone. Two Search features can't be reached with the band. Two player swipes jump videos and lose your place. Loads you backed out of still change the screen seconds later. The most urgent fix is cheap: opening "From iPhone" puts focus on "New code", and one extra pinch swaps the paired link for a new one. That fits the live "Playing on your glasses but nothing happens" report. The biggest UX gain is a navigation stack that remembers focus, plus a reworked Search (reachable recent queries, suggestions after 2-3 letters, typing on the phone) and a player menu on Down in place of instant next-video. Typing a query today costs about 3-5 inputs per character (33 on average, 59 for "taylor swift"). Reordering the grid doesn't help (332 vs 339/340 inputs over 10 queries); typing 3 letters and picking a suggestion takes 12-17.

findings.title: Pinch-ready 'New code' is the default focus on From iPhone and silently unpairs the phone
findings.evidence: Harness run 'phone': with a stored link 'durable-link-token', Down+Enter opens From iPhone and document.activeElement = btn-pair-new (screenshot audit/nav/phone-01-phone-screen-additive.png shows the red-ringed 'New code' pill while the help text says 'Phone connected'). One more pinch changed link to 'local-test-token' and the code from ABC123 to TESTQA. The click handler (app.js:1793-1800) calls linkStore('') and pairCodeStore(''), then newPairCode(), with no confirm. The phone keeps pushing to the old link while the glasses poll a new one. That matches live problem (1), 'phone says Playing on your glasses, nothing happens'. An EMG double-fire on the From iPhone row is enough to trigger it.
findings.recommendation: Make Back (or nothing) the default focus on screen-phone, and put New code last. Ask for confirmation: the first pinch changes the label to 'Pinch again to unlink your iPhone' for 3 s, and only a second pinch in that window calls newPairCode. Hide New code while pairState says paired and the link token exists, or move it under Diagnostics. Send a hudNote('unlink') so the server log shows when the glasses dropped a link.

findings.title: Search: recent-query chips can't be reached with the band; Left is not back; two focus highlights
findings.evidence: renderSearch builds .kb-recent-btn buttons without the 'focusable' class (app.js:1239-1250). moveKey walks only KEY_ROWS plus the action row (app.js:1208-1260), so the chips are mouse-only. The comment at app.js:1186-1189 says re-running a search 'should never cost 12 pinches', but it still does. In audit/nav/pl-02-search-up-from-row0-additive.png, Up from row 0 wraps to the 'Back' action key, not the LOFI / MKBHD IPHONE chips. handleSearchKey maps ArrowLeft to moveKey(0,-1) (app.js:1729), yet the bottom bar reads 'Back  swipe left' (index.html:172). That bar can't be reached either, and it is DOM-focused, so it draws a focus fill and red bar at the same time as the white grid cursor (search-02-search-open.png). The unfocused 'Search' key is also white (styles.css:833), the same as the focused key (styles.css:841), so three bright blocks compete. openSearch() clears typed (app.js:1279), so Left from results throws the query away (verified: typed='' after Back).
findings.recommendation: Treat the search screen as rows: [recent/suggestion chips] above [grid rows] above [actions]. Up from grid row 0 enters the chip row, Left/Right move along it, pinch runs that query. Re-running a query then costs Enter, Up, Enter. When the field is empty and the cursor is on the first chip (or on A), Left = back, which keeps Left as the global back gesture. Remove #btn-search-back; the 'Back' action key is enough, and the double highlight goes away. Make the unfocused Search key an outlined red key, not a white fill. Keep typed when returning from results and put the cursor on the Search key.

findings.title: Letter-grid typing costs ~4 inputs per character; the only real fix is prediction or the phone
findings.evidence: Live run: Search 'lofi' took Enter + 14 inputs for the letters + Down*4 + Enter, then Down + Enter on a result: 22 inputs to a video. A BFS over the real moveKey rules (scratch audit/nav/calc/grid.mjs) gives: lofi 16, mkbhd 20, ted talk 32, nasa live 46, veritasium 43, minecraft 47, taylor swift 59. Total 332 for 10 queries. A 7-wide alphabetical grid (339) and a frequency-centred grid (340) are no better, and dropping horizontal wrap costs 25% more (414). Typing 3 letters and then Up + pinch on a suggestion costs 12-17 for every one of those queries (taylor swift: 59 down to 14).
findings.recommendation: 1) Add /api/suggest (YouTube suggest endpoint, client=youtube) and show 3-4 suggestions in the chip row once 2 letters are typed, so Up + pinch runs one. 2) Add a 'search' push kind so the iPhone keyboard (or iOS dictation) can send a query; applyPush calls typed=q; runSearch(). On the phone screen, add 'Type on iPhone'. 3) Keep the 10x4 grid layout; changing it doesn't pay. 4) After each letter, keep the cursor where it is (as now). After 3+ letters, open the chip row so suggestions sit one Up away.

findings.title: Back never restores focus; from the player it lands on 'Play all', so one pinch restarts the list
findings.evidence: show() always calls focusFirst() (app.js:261, 280-288), and renderList rebuilds the DOM each time. Harness run 'chan': play Kurzgesagt's video #2, then Left gives active='Play all' (chan-05-back-from-player.png). Another Left gives active='TED Talks' (not Kurzgesagt, the channel you came from). Another Left gives home with focus on the first item. Settings, then Left, gives focus on 'Search', not Settings. After going back from the player, a pinch on Play all runs openPlayer(0) on the whole list and reshuffles it when shuffle is on (app.js:627-630). Search results, channel feeds and Recents also open with Play all focused, though the top result is usually what you want. Playlists play item 1 at once without showing their contents (app.js:1099-1106). Back from that player shows the contents, and the next Left skips the Playlists level and goes home (pl2 run: 'Morning mix' list, then home).
findings.recommendation: Add a real navigation stack: push {render fn, args, focusIndex, scrollTop} on every forward navigation, and have goBack() pop it and restore focus and scroll. When leaving the player, focus the row of the video that was playing and label it 'Resume · 12:34'. On search and channel lists, default focus to the first video row, not Play all. Make Playlists open the contents list (Play all + rows) the same way channels do.

findings.title: Player swipes: Down skips instantly, Up changes meaning, and next/prev throws away the resume point
findings.evidence: handlePlayerKey (app.js:1686-1718): Down always calls playNext(). Up calls playPrev() when queue>1 but Player.seek(-10) when the queue is a single video, so a queue has no way to rewind. playPrev on video 1 wraps to the last video. The hint reads 'Up last', which suggests the final item. playNext and playPrev call openPlayer without startAt (app.js:897-923). Instrumented run 'pk' logged Player.load calls [aircAruvnKk,312] then Down [ujkD4SxPKOI,0] then Up [aircAruvnKk,0,'proxy']. Coming back to a video with a stored 5:12 mark starts it at 0 on the first route. progressSave then calls markSet with t<10, which deletes the mark (app.js:159). So one stray Down followed by Up loses your place in a long video for good. Right is fixed at +10 s, with no acceleration (a 1-hour video needs up to 360 swipes to cross).
findings.recommendation: Player model: pinch = play/pause; Right = +10 s and Up = -10 s, the same in every queue, accelerating to 30 s then 60 s when repeated within 1 s; Left = back to the list with the resume row focused; Down = open a player menu (Next, Previous, Restart, Speed, Captions, Audio only, Up next). Skipping then takes 2 deliberate inputs. Pass resumeAt(id) in playNext and playPrev. If instant Down=next stays, show a 4 s toast 'Skipped · swipe up to go back to 12:34' that restores the position.

findings.title: Focus indicator is weak or ambiguous on the additive display
findings.evidence: Video rows show focus only as background #303030 plus a 5 px inset red bar (styles.css:334-341). On search-06-results-down12-additive.png the focused row is hard to pick out; the dark grey fill disappears on the see-through display. Rows without thumbnails (Channels, Playlists, Library, Subscriptions) all inherit the red 'Play all' pill (styles.css:279-311). Every row looks like a primary button, and focus is only a thin white ring (chan-02-channels-additive.png, pl2-02-playlists-focus-2-additive.png). The unfocused Continue card (#212121, styles.css:199) looks almost the same as a focused row (#303030) (rec-05-home-on-playlists.png). In Search the focused key is white with a dark letter, which turns transparent on additive (search-03-typed-lofi-additive.png).
findings.recommendation: Use brightness contrast, which survives additive blending: dim unfocused rows (opacity .55, or text #9a9a9a) and keep the focused row at full white, with a 3 px red outline around the whole row or thumbnail and an 8 px left bar. Use the red pill only for real actions (Play all); render channel and playlist rows like home rows. Make the focused grid key red with white text, and the Search key outlined. Give the unfocused Continue card no fill, only a thin outline.

findings.title: Ghost navigation: channel feeds and searches you backed out of still take over the screen
findings.evidence: Harness run 'ghost': Channels, pinch TED Talks, then Left twice puts the HUD on home. 5 s later current='list', title 'TED Talks', with no input. Run 'ghost2': start a NASA search, Left back to Search, type 'K'. Seconds later the HUD shows 'Search: NASA' over the keyboard (typed='K' was discarded). loadChannel only checks feedWait, and goBack never clears it (app.js:1146-1182). runSearch has no cancel token (app.js:1286-1310). Picking a channel shows no feedback on the row while it loads, only the status line, so pinching again or backing out is a natural reaction.
findings.recommendation: Add a navigation generation counter, incremented on every show() and goBack(), and drop any async result whose generation differs: if (gen !== myGen) return. Clear feedWait in goBack. While a feed or search loads, show a spinner and 'Loading…' on the picked row, and use Left to cancel it.

findings.title: Home order shifts under your thumb, and browsing a list overwrites the queue
findings.evidence: Continue, Queue and Library appear and disappear (renderHome, app.js:500-511). showVideoList sets queue = videos when you only open a list (app.js:621). In run 'rec', viewing Recents without playing added 'Queue · 14 videos · Recents' to home and pushed every item down one. The planned Down*6 to Playlists landed on Channels (rec-05-home-on-playlists.png). That also replaces the queue you were really playing. With Continue, Queue and Library showing, home has 10 rows, and Settings and Diagnostics sit below the fold with no scroll cue (rec-01-home-full-additive.png).
findings.recommendation: Only replace queue when a video starts (in openPlayer from a list), not when a list is rendered. Keep fixed slots: Continue (only when present, always first), Search, From iPhone, Recents, Channels, Playlists, Library, Settings. Fold Queue into the Continue card ('Continue · 3/14 Morning mix'). Move Diagnostics into Settings so home fits on one screen.

findings.title: Left on Home moves focus up and wraps to Diagnostics
findings.evidence: app.js:1756-1761: on home, ArrowLeft = moveFocus('up'). Settings run: Left from Settings lands on home with focus on 'Search'. One more Left (overshooting back) moves focus to 'Diagnostics' (wrap). A user who swipes Left repeatedly to 'get home' ends up on a random row, and the next pinch opens it.
findings.recommendation: Make Left on home do nothing, or show a brief 'Home' pulse on the title. Keep wrap for Up/Down only. Repeated Left then always settles safely on home with focus kept.

findings.title: Error recovery dead end: 'Play from the phone instead' can't be reached in the player
findings.evidence: #btn-relay is a .focusable button inside the player (index.html:160-162). In the player, handlePlayerKey never moves DOM focus, and pinch always calls Player.toggle (app.js:1693-1699). Run 'err2': after the blocked message and showRelayOffer(), Down then Enter left activeElement=BODY and the URL unchanged (err2-01-blocked-relay-additive.png shows the button on screen). The real no-play case in run 'err' sat on 'Enter to play' after 22 s; pinching did nothing visible.
findings.recommendation: In the blocked or error state, change the pinch target: the hint reads 'Pinch: play from phone · Swipe down: next video · Swipe left: back', and handlePlayerKey sends Enter to openRelay() when the relay offer is visible. After N pinches with no playback, show an explicit 'This video won't play here' with the same choices.

findings.title: No in-player controls; changing speed, captions or audio-only means leaving and rebuffering
findings.evidence: Settings is reachable only from home (index.html:127). Player.destroy() runs when you leave the player (app.js:245-248). Counted path while watching: Left, Left, Up*2 (via wrap), pinch Settings, Down*2, pinch Speed, Left, pinch Continue. That is 10 inputs, and the route chain restarts, so the video may hit the 'Enter to play' gate again. Speed cycles forward only (prefs.js SPEEDS), so going down one step from 1.5x takes 3 pinches.
findings.recommendation: Use the Down player menu (see the player finding) for Speed, Captions, Audio only and the sleep timer, applied live through Player.applyAll() without destroying playback. In menus, Right = next value and pinch = next value. Return focus to the same row after a change.

findings.title: Long lists: focus pinned to the bottom edge, no position count, Right wasted, Back is a dead stop
findings.evidence: reveal() uses scrollIntoView({block:'nearest'}) (app.js:276). Scrolling down keeps the focused row at the bottom edge with no preview of the next row (search-06-results-down12.png, row 13 of 21). There is no 'n of N' indicator. Right does the same as Down (app.js:1764). Up from the first row wraps to the bottom 'Back swipe left' button (rec-04-recents-up-wrap.png), which only repeats what Left does. Search returns 20 results (app.js:1293) with no 'More results' row.
findings.recommendation: Scroll with block:'center' so one or two rows of look-ahead stay visible. Add a '7/20' counter to the right of the list title. Make Right page down 5 rows (or 'Play next' on a video row). Remove the Back buttons from focus order (Left is back everywhere), so the wrap goes last row to first row. Add a final 'More results' row that fetches the next 20.

findings.title: Gesture hints mix keyboard words with band words and are missing where they matter
findings.evidence: Player hint: 'Enter play · Up last · Down next · Left back · Right +10s' (index.html:158, app.js:1020-1022). Gates say 'Enter to play'. List back bars say 'swipe left'. Home has no hint. Search has no hint for pinch-to-type, and its one 'swipe left' hint is wrong. There are no physical keys on the glasses, so 'Enter' doesn't mean anything to the wearer.
findings.recommendation: Use one vocabulary with glyphs: 'Pinch play/pause · ↑ −10s · → +10s · ↓ menu · ← back'. Show the player hint for 4 s after load or after any input, then fade it. Add a one-line footer on Home ('↑↓ move · pinch open') and on Search ('pinch types · ↑ recent').

findings.title: Long-press and double-pinch are unmeasured; add an input-capture test before designing for them
findings.evidence: Only keydown is handled (app.js:1741-1766), with no keyup, e.repeat or timing. Whether the Neural Band sends keyup on pinch release, key repeat while held, or distinct codes is unknown. An Enter that fires twice already carries risk (it pauses right after opening).
findings.recommendation: Add 'Input test' to Diagnostics: log key, code, repeat, and keydown-to-keyup ms for 20 events, and post them to /api/diag. If hold is detectable (keyup delta > 500 ms), map pinch-hold = player menu or 'go Home'. Don't build on double-pinch, because it delays every single pinch by about 300 ms. Ignore repeated keydowns (e.repeat) for Enter so an accidental double fire doesn't activate twice.

audits.area: Visual design and legibility on the additive display
audits.summary: The HUD copies YouTube's dark phone look: dark grey fills (#212121, #272727, #303030), a 5px pure-red focus bar, 12-14px secondary text, and white pills with black text. Most of that fails on see-through additive optics. Dim greys add almost no light, pure red is only about 21% as bright as white, and black text on a white pill shows up as a hole cut into a bright block. The worst problem is a CSS cascade bug. On every video row (search results, channel videos, Recents, Queue) it cancels the focus fill, so you cannot tell which video a pinch will play. I measured almost no brightness difference between focused and unfocused rows. A second selector bug turns every Channel and Playlist row into a red call-to-action pill. The biggest opportunity is one focus language plus a type floor: a 3px white ring, dimmed thumbnails on unfocused rows, nothing below 16px or weight 500, and red only for brand and progress. I prototyped this as an injected stylesheet with no repo edits (audit/visual/proto/proposal.css). It fixes focus visibility on home, lists, search and the player in the additive composites. Two UX traps also stand out because they relate to the live problems. On From iPhone, focus starts on "New code", so one extra pinch silently unlinks the phone. The home screen also never shows whether a phone is linked.

findings.title: Focus is invisible on every video row (CSS cascade cancels the focus style)
findings.evidence: styles.css:716-727 `.list-btn:has(.list-shot){background:transparent;color:#f1f1f1}` has the same specificity (0,2,0) as `.focusable:focus` (styles.css:334-339) and comes later, so it cancels the #303030 focus fill and the #fff text. styles.css:729 `.list-btn:has(.list-shot) small{color:#c9c9c9}` likewise cancels :340. Only `box-shadow: inset 5px 0 0 #ff0000` is left: a 5px pure-red strip at x=16-21, next to a bright thumbnail. Measured mean luminance of the focused row's text area vs the same row unfocused: 20.0 vs 19.3 (raw), 95.1 vs 94.9 (additive), so effectively zero. Seen in audit/visual/results-row4.png, results-row10-additive.png (the focused Xiaomi row cannot be picked out) and chan-v6-additive.png. This affects search results, channel video lists, Recents and Queue: the main way to choose a video.
findings.recommendation: Give focus one style and make it win the cascade (put it after the row rules or raise specificity): `.focusable:focus, .list-btn:has(.list-shot):focus { background: transparent; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 3px #fff; border-radius: 14px; color: #fff; }` and `.focusable:focus small { color: #dcdcdc; }`. Add a second cue that also cuts glare: `.list-shot img { opacity: .5 } .list-btn:focus .list-shot img { opacity: 1 }`. Checked on the additive composite in audit/visual/proto/p-results-additive.png and p-results-linear.png: the focused row is obvious.

findings.title: Channels and Playlists show as a column of red call-to-action pills
findings.evidence: styles.css:279-311 `.list-btn:not(:has(img))` was meant for the 'Play all' action. It matches every list row that has no thumbnail, which includes every channel row (openChannels) and every playlist row (openPlaylists, app.js:1094-1108). Each gets background #ff0000, radius 20px, 16px/700 text, a 13px #ffdede sub line and shrink-to-fit width. audit/visual/lists-channels.png shows six identical red pills, and lists-channels-2-additive.png shows they are the brightest objects on screen. Focus is only a 3px white ring on one of six identical slabs, so every row reads as a primary button. Playlists has the same bug (after2-playlists.png). The repeated 'Latest videos' sub line on every channel adds noise and no information.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit class for the action row in showVideoList (app.js:618-637), e.g. `.list-btn.is-action`, and scope the pill styling to it. Render channel and playlist rows as plain 62px text rows: label 20px/600 #fff, sub 16px/500 #a8a8a8, the standard 3px white ring on focus. Replace 'Latest videos' with real information (video count or last upload) or drop it. Prototype: audit/visual/proto/p-channels-additive.png.

findings.title: The global focus style is too weak for additive optics (dark fill plus red sliver)
findings.evidence: styles.css:334-339: focus is background #303030 plus `inset 5px 0 0 #ff0000`. #303030 has relative luminance 0.03 (3% of white), so on see-through optics it is a faint tint that vanishes over bright parts of the room. In home-0-additive.png the focused 'Search' row sits over the window and can barely be told apart. #ff0000 has luminance 0.21, about a fifth of white text, so the 5px bar reads as a dull salmon strip at the far left edge. Row separators #272727 (styles.css:192, 217) have luminance 0.02 and are invisible, so they add nothing. #btn-pair-new focus (styles.css:667-670) is a red-only 3px ring on #3f3f3f. Caveat: the harness's additive images overstate these greys (see the last finding). The linear re-blend home-3-linear.png shows the fill even fainter.
findings.recommendation: Use one focus style on every screen: a 3px #fff ring (`box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 3px #fff; border-radius: 14px`) with the label at #fff. Unfocused labels stay #fff (primary) or #dcdcdc (secondary). Never signal state with a fill or with red alone. Delete the #272727 separators and separate rows with 4-8px gaps. Keep red for the brand mark, progress fills and the single Play-all CTA. Prototype home: audit/visual/proto/p-home-additive.png.

findings.title: Dark-on-white elements turn inside out on the additive display (letters become holes)
findings.evidence: The search cursor `.kb-key.kb-on{background:#fff;color:#0f0f0f}` (styles.css:841-846), the Search key `.kb-key.kb-go{background:#fff;color:#0f0f0f}` (833-837, white at all times) and the play-gate pill `.play-gate-msg{background:#fff;color:#0f0f0f}` (489-494) all use black text on white. Black emits no light, so each letter becomes a see-through hole in a bright slab. In search-actions-additive.png the room shows through the focused 'X' and the 'Search' label. In player-t3-additive.png the letters of 'Enter to play' are the brown background. The white Search key is a permanent 138x44 bright block in the user's view.
findings.recommendation: Reverse the treatment: transparent fill, white text, and a ring for state. Cursor: `.kb-key.kb-on{background:transparent;color:#fff;border-color:#fff;box-shadow:inset 0 0 0 2px #fff;transform:scale(1.06)}`. Search key: `background:transparent;border:2px solid #ff3d3d;color:#fff`, filled red only while the cursor is on it. Play gate: `background:transparent;border:3px solid #fff;color:#fff;font-size:20px;padding:10px 26px;border-radius:28px`. Checked in audit/visual/proto/p-search-additive.png and p-player-paused-linear.png.

findings.title: From iPhone: one pinch silently unlinks the phone, and linked state is never shown
findings.evidence: index.html:188 'New code' is the first .focusable on the screen, so show() -> focusFirst() focuses it on entry (eval: document.activeElement.id = 'btn-pair-new'; phone-pair.png shows the red ring on it). Its handler (app.js:1793) clears the durable link (linkStore('')) and mints a new code. A double pinch from home therefore moves the glasses to a new pairing while the phone keeps pushing to the old one. That fits live problem 1 ('Playing on your glasses', nothing happens). When paired, the screen still shows the big code and the 'Type this code' steps under 'Phone connected...' (paired-phone-additive.png), which contradicts itself. The home row reads 'Code TESTQA · listening' whether a phone is linked or not (updateHomePhoneHint, app.js:493-498). paired-home.png and home-0.png are identical.
findings.recommendation: Focus Back (or a harmless row) by default. Move 'Pair a different phone' to the last row and make it a two-step confirm ('Pinch again to unlink'). Paired view: large 'iPhone linked' in #4ff08f with a check glyph, the last pushed title and how long ago, and the code demoted to 18px. Home header: a link chip ('● iPhone linked' green / '○ Not linked' #a8a8a8), and change the row sub line to 'Linked · last video 2m ago'.

findings.title: Search screen: unreachable recent-query chips, a false back hint, two focus indicators
findings.evidence: The recent-query chips (.kb-recent-btn, styles.css:785-797; rendered at app.js:1240-1250) are not part of keyGrid(), and moveKey only walks KEY_ROWS + KEY_ACTIONS, so the band can never reach them (srch2-chips.png). Typing with a band is slow, and these chips are the only shortcut. handleSearchKey (app.js:1720-1739) maps ArrowLeft to cursor movement, yet the footer says 'Back swipe left' (index.html:172). That footer button also keeps DOM focus the whole time, so it shows the grey fill and red bar while the grid cursor is elsewhere (search-typed.png: the P key and Back both look focused). Up from the top row wraps onto the action row and lands on 'Back', where one pinch throws away the query.
findings.recommendation: Make the chips row 0 of the grid so the cursor can reach them. Blur DOM focus on entering search, and replace the footer with a non-focusable hint ('Back key, bottom-left'), or remove it. Reorder the actions to Search | Delete | Space | Back, or make the wrap land on Search, so a stray Up+pinch submits instead of exiting.

findings.title: Type is too small and too light for a see-through HUD
findings.evidence: 12px: #player-time (styles.css:594), .list-dur (699). 13px: #player-hint (617), pill sub line (304), #debug-log (644). 14px: every secondary line, including .menu-btn small (266), #player-channel (557), #player-next (604), .status (366), .errbar (388), .kb-recent-btn (792), .back-hint (331) and .splash-credit (114). Primary labels are only 16-18px at weight 400-500 (173, 254). If the display is about 20° diagonal (roughly 42 px/deg), 14px Roboto has a cap height near 14 arcmin and 12px near 12 arcmin. That is small for glance reading with a busy world behind it. In the linear composites, 14px #c9c9c9 sub lines fade out over the bright window. The player's own control hint is the smallest text on screen (13px inside an invisible #212121 box).
findings.recommendation: Floor: no text under 16px, no weight under 500, no text colour darker than #a8a8a8. Scale: screen title 26/700 #fff; home row label 21/600; list row label 20/600; video title 18/600, 2-line clamp, line-height 1.25; secondary 16/500 #dcdcdc; hint 16/500 #a8a8a8; time and badges 16/600 with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; player title 22/700; pair code 64/800 letter-spacing 12px; keyboard letters 26/600.

findings.title: Adopt one token-based visual system for additive optics
findings.evidence: Colours are hard-coded per rule with 14 different greys (#f1f1f1, #e6e6e6, #eee, #c9c9c9, #8d8d8d, #3f3f3f, #303030, #2f2f2f, #272727, #212121, #1c1c1c, #1a1a1a, #0f0f0f, #fff), and several of them render as nothing on the glasses. Screens disagree on structure: home uses separators, Continue uses a #212121 card, Settings puts values at the far right, lists use pills or thumbnails, and From iPhone mixes centred and left-aligned text. A prototype override validated across home, lists, search, settings and the player: audit/visual/proto/proposal.css and the p-*-additive.png images.
findings.recommendation: Tokens: --bg:#000; --t1:#fff (titles, labels); --t2:#dcdcdc (secondary); --t3:#a8a8a8 (hints only, at least 16px); --accent:#ff3d3d (brand, progress, the Play-all CTA; slightly brighter than #ff0000); --focus:#fff; --ok:#4ff08f; --err:#ff7a70. No fills darker than #5e5e5e except pure black; express structure with spacing, outlines and opacity, not dark cards. Focus: 3px #fff ring, radius 14px. Spacing: 8px grid, 24px side inset, 20px top. Rows: home 62px; text rows 62px (20/600 + 16/500); video rows 96px with a 144x81 thumbnail (radius 10) and a 14px gap. Keys 56px. Pills only for the one primary action per screen.

findings.title: Player: permanent text clutter below the video, a 3px progress bar, 12px time over bright video
findings.evidence: The video is pinned to the top at 600x338 (styles.css:409-426). Title, channel, Next and hint (537-624) stay rendered below it the whole time it plays, about 260px of text laid over the world (play2-playing-additive.png). The title is also duplicated in the gate and in the meta block (player-t3.png). The progress bar is 3px with an rgba(255,255,255,.24) track (567-585); the track is about 5% luminance in linear light and the 3px red fill is dim. #player-time is 12px with a black text-shadow (594-598), and black shadows emit nothing on additive, so the time sits directly on bright video. 'Next:' is hard-cut at 44 characters with no ellipsis (app.js:1025, giving '...Never Gonna Give You Up (Offic').
findings.recommendation: While playing, show only the video, vertically centred (top 131px), plus a 4px progress line. Any swipe reveals an overlay for 3s, then fades it: title 22/700 above the video; a 6px bar (track rgba(255,255,255,.35), fill #ff3d3d, 12px white playhead); time 16/600 below the bar; one hint line at 16px. Use CSS ellipsis instead of slice(0,44). Keep the existing 55% black scrim under the gates (452), which usefully dims the poster.

findings.title: Thumbnails: small, all at full brightness; the duration badge is illegible and duplicated
findings.evidence: Thumbnails are 128x72 (styles.css:237-242, 675-690), about 3.0°x1.7°. Every thumbnail renders at full brightness, so four or five bright rectangles per screen compete with the focused row and wash out the room (results-list-additive.png). .list-dur depends on an rgba(0,0,0,.85) backing (697), which is transparent on additive, leaving 12px white digits on a bright image. The same duration is already in the sub line ('Marques Brownlee · 14:13 · 7.3M · 4d ago'). The 3px red .list-seen bar (705-712) joins the red focus bar into an 'L' shape (after2-recents.png).
findings.recommendation: 144x81 (or 160x90) thumbnails with radius 10. Unfocused opacity .5, focused 1. Remove .list-dur. Sub line = 'Channel · 14:13 · 35% watched' (drop view counts). Watched-progress bar 5px #ff3d3d.

findings.title: Wasted space and low density on home, lists and search
findings.evidence: Home's last row ends at y≈474, leaving about 126px of black (home-0.png), while Continue and Queue push Diagnostics below the fold, and Settings plus Diagnostics take 2 of the 7 visible slots. Every screen reserves 40px of bottom padding (styles.css:35) for a status bar that is usually hidden, plus a 44-52px Back row (313-329): about 92px of permanent chrome. Video rows are 88px, so only 4.5 are visible. The search grid ends at y≈352 and leaves about 160px empty under 46px keys (search-typed.png).
findings.recommendation: Move Diagnostics into Settings. Replace the full-width Back row with a single 16px footer line ('← Back'); keep a focusable Back only where ArrowLeft is not back (search). Drop the 40px status padding and float the status as a toast instead. Home rows 62px; keys 56px with the field at 26px, which fills the free space with larger targets.

findings.title: Scrolling hard-clips rows at the edges and parks focus on the bottom edge
findings.evidence: reveal() uses scrollIntoView({block:'nearest'}) (app.js:276), so the focused row hugs the bottom of the list and the next row is cut mid-thumbnail. Scrolled lists also leave slivers under the title: results-row10-additive.png has a cut row under 'Search: MKBHD', and chan-v6-additive.png shows the Play-all ring peeking out at y≈55.
findings.recommendation: Use block:'center', or keep focus as the second visible row, with scroll-padding 24px. Add `mask-image: linear-gradient(transparent, #000 24px, #000 calc(100% - 28px), transparent)` on .screen-body so cut rows fade out instead of being sliced.

findings.title: On-screen copy uses keyboard words; the wearer pinches
findings.evidence: 'Enter to play' (index.html:151; app.js:860, 1018, 1064-1066), 'Enter pause' (app.js:1013), 'Paused · Enter play', and 'Up last · Down next · Left back · Right +10s' (index.html:158). On the glasses there is no Enter key: the action is a pinch on the Neural Band.
findings.recommendation: 'Pinch to play', 'Pinch to pause'; for directions, arrow glyphs '↑ prev  ↓ next  ← back  → +10s'. Use the same vocabulary on every screen.

findings.title: The search field hides the letters just typed
findings.evidence: .kb-text (styles.css:754-769) uses white-space:nowrap with text-overflow:ellipsis, which cuts the END of the query: 'MKBHD IPHONE 18 PRO REVIEW CAMERA TE…' (srch2-long.png). The cut part is exactly what was just entered. There is no caret. The placeholder is #8d8d8d 16px on a #212121 box (771-776), and the box is invisible on additive.
findings.recommendation: Show the tail of the query (render the last ~22 characters with a leading '…' in JS). Add a blinking 2px white caret. Make the field transparent with a 2px #8a8a8a underline, text 26px/700, placeholder 20px #a8a8a8.

findings.title: The error bar covers the header; the status toast is small and out of context
findings.evidence: .errbar (styles.css:376-391) is absolutely positioned at top:0 over the header, hiding the logo and 'GlassTube' (after2-errbar-offline-additive.png); its text is 14px #ff8983. .status (356-370) is 14px at the very bottom edge (y≈566-600). After openQueue() it showed 'Nothing queued.' beneath the Recents list, where it does not belong (after2-queue.png).
findings.recommendation: Use one toast component: 16px/600 at a 24px inset, above the footer, with a 3px left rule in #ff7a70 for errors, auto-hidden after 5s. The error bar should push content down or appear as a toast rather than cover the title.

findings.title: No build or freshness indicator on home
findings.evidence: The build ('1.25', index.html:70) appears only on the Diagnostics screen. Given live problem 2 (old pages stay in memory for days), the wearer cannot tell at a glance whether the glasses are running the current HUD.
findings.recommendation: Show a 16px #a8a8a8 'v1.25' right-aligned in the home header next to the link chip. When a newer build is detected, show an 'Update ready · pinch to reload' row at the top of home.

findings.title: Settings, empty states and the Continue card have weak hierarchy
findings.evidence: Settings values (.list-settings small, styles.css:220-226) are 16px/400 #c9c9c9, pushed about 450px away from their labels by space-between, and nothing signals that a pinch cycles the value (settings-settings-back.png). The Recents and Playlists empty states are one 16px line followed by about 400px of void, with only Back focusable (lists-recents-empty-additive.png). 'Searching...' has no spinner. The Continue card (199-207) inverts the hierarchy: 'Continue' is 18px while the actual video title is 14px grey; it has no thumbnail, and the red inset bar is clipped by the 12px radius (play2-after-back.png).
findings.recommendation: Settings values 20px/700 #fff, with '‹ 1x ›' chevrons when focused. Give each empty state a focused action row ('Open Channels', 'Pair iPhone'). Reuse the player spinner for Searching. Continue card = 144x81 thumbnail + title 18/600 + 'Resume at 3:12 · 35%'.

findings.title: The harness's additive preview overstates dim greys (blends in gamma space)
findings.evidence: shot.mjs:145 composites with globalCompositeOperation 'lighter' on sRGB-encoded values, so #303030 adds 48/255 (19%) even though its linear luminance is 3%. Re-blending the same screenshots in linear light (audit/visual/tools/linear.py -> *-linear.png) shows the key fills (#1c1c1c), cards (#212121) and separators disappearing entirely and the focus fill far fainter: compare search-typed-additive.png with search-typed-linear.png.
findings.recommendation: Switch the harness to a linear blend (decode both images to linear, add, re-encode) so later audits judge dim fills the way the optics actually add light.

audits.area: Video player experience (player.js, player parts of app.js, styles.css, index.html #screen-player)
audits.summary: The video already uses the most space a 16:9 picture can at 600 wide (600x338, 56% of the screen). But it is pinned to the top, the text under it never hides, and the time and progress bar drawn over the picture are too small to read on the see-through display. The biggest defect is starting playback. player.js builds a new <video> for every video and unmutes it the moment muted autoplay starts. Chrome pauses a muted autoplay that gets unmuted without a gesture, and under the glasses WebView's default autoplay rule a new element can't play at all without one. So every push, and every next video in a queue, stops at "Enter to play". Then the 12s stall timer drops the working phone-file route while that prompt is still waiting, and the player ends on an endless "Loading..." with no error. That is a credible cause of "the phone says playing but nothing happens on the glasses". Separately, player.js reads window.GlassPrefs and window.GlassSound, which don't exist, so Speed, Sound Off, Audio only and Captions are all ignored during playback. The single biggest opportunity: keep one <video> element for the whole session, unlock it on the first pinch, never unmute without a gesture, and never drop a route while waiting for a pinch. In headless Chrome under the WebView rule, a reused, unlocked element played later videos with sound and no pinch, while a new element was refused. None of these fixes reach the glasses until the page reloads (known issue 2).

findings.title: Every push and every queued video stops at 'Enter to play': a new <video> per video, plus unmuting right after muted autoplay starts
findings.evidence: player.js:532-582 mountVideo creates a brand-new <video> each time (slot.innerHTML='' then createElement). Its 'playing' listener (546-551) calls applySound(), which unmutes with no user gesture, and tryPlay (203-208) ignores why play() was rejected. Measured in headless Chrome with my harness copy (audit/player/shotp.mjs, serving a local MP4 as the googlevideo 'u'): (1) Default policy, media events logged: 'play@0.00 muted | playing@0.00 muted | volumechange@0.00 unmuted', then time froze at 0.006s and the gate appeared (docact2 and docact runs). (2) --autoplay-policy=user-gesture-required, the Android WebView default: I pinched to play video 1/2 using a key press only (no evals, since Playwright's evaluate counts as a gesture). When video 1 ended naturally, video 2/2 sat at time 0.0007 with the 'Enter to play' gate (qclean-b2-additive.png, state b3). (3) unlock/index.html test under user-gesture-required: one <video> primed by play() inside the first keydown later played unmuted after src swaps with no gesture, twice. A newly created element got NotAllowedError. Log: 'new-element NotAllowedError | prime ok | same-element unmuted play OK | same-element 2nd swap OK'. Matches known issue 3.
findings.recommendation: 1) Create one persistent <video id=yt-host> once and reuse it for every html5 route. load() swaps v.src; resetSoft() does pause(), removeAttribute('src'), load() but keeps the element. Put the embed/go iframes in a sibling container so they never replace the video. 2) Unlock it: in the capture-phase keydown listener (app.js:1741), on the first key of the session call v.muted=false; v.play().catch(()=>{}) synchronously. After that, pushes and queue advances autoplay with sound for the life of the page, which on the glasses is days. 3) In tryPlay, read the play() promise. On NotAllowedError, try once muted. If muted playback runs, stay muted, show a small 'Sound off · pinch for sound' chip and unmute only inside the next keydown. If muted also fails, show the gate immediately (not after 3.2s), stop retries and route timers, and send hudNote('autoplay-blocked'). 4) Remove the unconditional applySound() from the 'playing' listener. Unmute only when navigator.userActivation.isActive is true or the element is known to be unlocked.

findings.title: The stall timer drops the working phone-file route while 'Enter to play' waits, and timers left from an earlier attempt fire into a fresh one; ends at an endless 'Loading...'
findings.evidence: app.js:863-874: the 12s check calls tryNextWay() before it tests needGesture (line 871: `if (!tryNextWay(...) && !needGesture)`), so it advances the route even while the gate is showing. Strict run: hud-report 'stalled route:file gate:true', then route proxy (403), embed, go. After a pinch on the go route the state stayed 'Loading...' and no error ever appeared (fail run: state t31 gate, afterEnter14 'Loading...'). Cross-origin go and embed iframes never report an error, and the chain has no final timeout. The timer guards (850-866) compare only video id and wayPos, so re-opening the same video within 12s inherits the old timers. resend2 run: a second push of the same video got 'stalled route:file' about 5s in and was moved to proxy. Left then Continue showed the same thing (left run). Likely real-world sequence: user sends from the phone, looks up 5-10s later, the file route is gone, and they re-send, which makes it worse. updateChrome (1069-1071) also overwrites 'Trying server...' with 'Loading...' within 400ms, so the wearer never sees progress.
findings.recommendation: Give each openPlayer call its own id (const openId=++openSeq) and have every setTimeout return early unless openId===openSeq. Never call tryNextWay while needGesture is set or after a NotAllowedError. For <video> routes, decide a stall from network evidence, not the clock: v.error, networkState===NETWORK_NO_SOURCE, or no 'progress' event and no growth in buffered for 10s. If buffered is growing, wait. Once the chain is exhausted, or an iframe route reports no state for 20s after a pinch, show a final error. Base it on the most informative failure: a file-route 403 should read 'Your glasses aren't on the same WiFi as your phone', not the last route's text. Keep one stable loading line in the bottom band, e.g. 'Getting video from your phone… (2 of 4)', instead of flashing route names.

findings.title: Speed, Sound Off, Audio only and Captions are ignored during playback: player.js reads window.GlassPrefs and window.GlassSound, which are top-level consts and never on window
findings.evidence: prefs.js:1 `const GlassPrefs` and sound.js:1 `const GlassSound` are not window properties. player.js:61-67 uses window.GlassSound and window.GlassPrefs, so prefs() is always null and soundOn() is always true. In-page check after setAudioOnly(true), setSpeed(2) and setEnabled(false): [typeof window.GlassPrefs, typeof window.GlassSound, typeof GlassPrefs] = ['undefined','undefined','object']. The playing video then reported playbackRate 1, muted false, #yt-wrap class '' and the poster hidden. audio-z1-audio-additive.png shows full video in Audio-only mode. The Settings screen still shows the chosen values, so the HUD looks correct while doing the opposite. Sound Off also gets undone on every 'playing' event.
findings.recommendation: In player.js use `typeof GlassPrefs !== 'undefined' ? GlassPrefs : null` (and the same for GlassSound), as app.js:42-43 already does, or set window.GlassPrefs and window.GlassSound in prefs.js and sound.js. Add a selftest assertion that playbackRate, muted and the audio-only class match prefs after a file-route play.

findings.title: Player layout: video pinned to the top, text that never hides, 12px time and 3px bar over the video, status line that never clears
findings.evidence: styles.css:409-415 puts #yt-wrap at 0..338. Below it, title 18px, channel 14px, next 14px and a hint panel (13px #c9c9c9 on #212121, styles.css:613-624) stay lit the whole time. Nothing auto-hides. #player-time is 12px white with a text-shadow, which can't darken on an additive display (styles.css:587-599). #player-bar is 3px with a red fill that disappears over red video (file-p5-seek.png). The global #status keeps 'Playing from your phone.' or 'End of list.' at y≈580 for the whole session (file-p3-playing-8s-additive.png, end-x1-ended-additive.png). It even contradicts the gate ('Enter to play' plus 'Playing from your phone.', strict-s1-additive.png). Paused and gate states print the title twice, once over the video and once below. The rows from y≈470 to 560 are empty.
findings.recommendation: Use a 600x600 player with black (transparent) bands. Video: 600x338 at top:131 (centred). Chrome shows on load, on any key, on pause or error, and while buffering for more than 1s, and hides 3s after playback resumes. When hidden, only the video is lit. Top band (y 22-118): title 22px/700 white, 2 lines; subline 16px #d6d6d6 with 'Channel · 1 of 2 · 1.5x · Sleep 12m'. Bottom band (y 484-576), inset 24px: a 6px bar (white fill, rgba(255,255,255,.28) track, 16px red knob); a row with time at 18px/500 on the left and 'Next: …' at 16px on the right; a 15px gesture legend shown only on pause and in the first sessions. Never draw text over the video except a dimmed centre glyph or toast. Clear #status after 3s, and hide it while the player is showing. Mocks in audit/player/mock/index.html, checked through the same additive blend (mock-m1-chrome-additive.png, mock-m3-paused-additive.png). If centring feels wrong for Mike's eye line on the real glasses, keep the video at the top and move both bands below it. Auto-hide and the type sizes matter more than position.

findings.title: Left exits immediately, and a phone push can't be resumed on the phone-file route afterwards (the file URL is removed from Continue)
findings.evidence: handlePlayerKey (app.js:1688-1691): Left calls goBack(), which destroys the player. For 'From iPhone' it goes straight to home (app.js:515-524). progressSave deletes u from every queue row (app.js:380-385), and recentsAdd never stores it. Left run: after one Left swipe at 0:08, Continue rebuilt the chain as 'proxy>embed>go' with hasU:false, and the HUD sat at 'Loading...'. Per HANDOFF, proxy gets LOGIN_REQUIRED on Vercel, so on the glasses an accidental thumb swipe usually means re-sending from the phone. README says 'Left back (or previous if you just started a video)', which isn't implemented.
findings.recommendation: Guard Left. The first Left shows the chrome and a toast 'Swipe left again to leave' for 2.5s; a second Left exits. Keep u in memory only, in a map from id to {u, expire} (expire is in the googlevideo URL), and reuse it in openContinue, Recents and the queue while expire is in the future. After a phone push, return to a 'Now playing' queue list rather than home, so one pinch resumes.

findings.title: Controls: Up means different things depending on queue length, no visual seek feedback, keyboard words instead of gestures
findings.evidence: app.js:1707-1712: Up means previous video when the queue has more than one item, otherwise -10s. So a queue can't rewind, and Up on item 1 wraps to the last item (playPrev, 917-924). Right +10s changes only the 12px time (file-p5-seek.png shows 0:28 with no toast). Down on a single video only changes the bottom status to 'End of list.' (end run). The hint text says 'Enter pause · Up last · Down next · Left back · Right +10s'; 'last' is ambiguous, and the wearer pinches and swipes rather than pressing Enter or arrows.
findings.recommendation: Mapping: pinch = play/pause (and unmute if muted); Right = +10s; Up = -10s always, except in the first 5s of a queued video, where it goes to the previous video (what the README promises); Down = next, with a 'Next: title' toast or an in-player 'No next video'; Left = guarded exit. Show a centred seek toast ('+10s', 40px/800 on a rgba(0,0,0,.6) pill), merge quick repeats ('+30s'), and show the bar with the new time for 900ms (mock-m4-seek-additive.png). Word the hints in gestures: 'pinch pause · ▶ +10s · ▲ −10s · ▼ next · ◀ exit'.

findings.title: Gate and pause overlay: a white pill (brightest thing on screen, text drawn in black) over a blurry upscaled poster
findings.evidence: .play-gate-msg (styles.css:489-494) is a #fff pill with #0f0f0f text. On an additive display the pill is the brightest light on screen and the letters are see-through holes ('Enter to play' and 'Ended · Enter to play' in strict-s1-additive.png and end-x1-ended-additive.png). The 18px title over a bright poster washes out ('Gorilla vs Grizzly Debate is Ins…' over the white gorilla, single-t1-loading-additive.png). The phone's default thumb is mqdefault 320x180 (ios Models.swift:25), stretched to 600x338, so the poster is visibly pixelated during loading, the gate and audio-only.
findings.recommendation: Dim the picture with filter: brightness(.4) on the video or poster, which lowers the light it gives off, instead of laying a 55% black layer over the title. Draw a 64px ▶ or ❚❚ glyph and a red #ff1a1a pill with white 22px/700 text reading 'Pinch to play' (mock-m5-gate-additive.png). Keep the title in the top band only. For the poster, use hq720.jpg or sddefault.jpg, falling back to hqdefault.

findings.title: No captions on the main (file) route; the empty band below the video is the right place for them
findings.evidence: applyCaptions returns early for html5 (player.js:156), so the file and proxy routes, which are what plays on the glasses, never show captions. On embed they are also off because of the GlassPrefs bug. README says 'embed routes only'. There is no <track> and no timedtext anywhere (grep).
findings.recommendation: Have the phone include the caption track baseUrl from the player response it already resolves (captionTracks[].baseUrl&fmt=vtt) in the push, or add a proxy endpoint. Parse the VTT in the HUD and draw cues yourself in the bottom band (y≈486-570), centred, 23px/600 white, at most 2 lines and about 42 characters per line, never over the picture (mock-m6-captions-additive.png). When the chrome shows, move the captions to the top band or hide them for those 3s.

findings.title: Error screen: three lines of red text squeezed under the video, a 'Play from the phone' button you can't reach, and the less useful error shown
findings.evidence: err-e1-error-additive.png: a 15px #ff8983 paragraph sits between the hint panel and the status line. The 'Play from the phone instead' button (index.html:160-162) has class .focusable, but in the player Enter always calls Player.toggle (app.js:1693-1699) and focus never moves, so the Neural Band can't activate it. playFailNote stores every route's error, but the message on screen comes from whichever route failed last.
findings.recommendation: For a final error, replace the video area with a centred 20px message and at most two actions mapped to gestures (e.g. 'Pinch: play from phone · Down: next video · Left: back'), and handle them in handlePlayerKey while blockedFor===nowPlaying.id. Pick the message from the most informative error in the chain: file 403 means a different WiFi or public IP, an expired file means 'Send it again from your phone', and an iPhone app that is too old says so.

findings.title: Long queues and old pushes lose the phone file: only the first 8 videos get one, it expires after hours, and the HUD never asks for a new one
findings.evidence: ios/GlassTube/WebScreen.swift:1334 `let n = min(videos.count, 8)`: a 'send all 20' push carries u only for items 1-8. The HUD never checks the googlevideo expire= parameter, so a queue played hours later tries an expired file, gets a media error, and falls through proxy, embed and go, which (per the finding above) can end at a gate or 'Loading...'. prefetchNext (app.js:881-891) only warms the server route.
findings.recommendation: When the next video has no file or an expiring one (less than 10 minutes left), the HUD asks the phone for a fresh one over the pair channel (a 'need' message the phone answers with a new push), two videos ahead. Show 'Next video needs your phone' instead of silently falling back.

findings.title: Vertical videos (Shorts) render at 190x338 inside the 16:9 box
findings.evidence: short-y1-short.png: a 9:16 file plays at 190x338 in the 600x338 box (styles.css:417-426, object-fit: contain inside a fixed 600x338). The other ~70% of the screen stays black.
findings.recommendation: For html5 routes make the video box 600x600 with object-fit: contain. 16:9 then gets 600x338 centred and 9:16 gets 338x600, about 3.2x the area. Put the chrome on the sides or overlay it briefly for portrait video.

findings.title: End of video and queue: no up-next countdown, Repeat defaults to All (loops forever), and 'Ended' leaves the gate and status up
findings.evidence: prefs.js default repeat 'all'. A 2-video push loops forever ('Next: Gorilla…' while on item 2/2, qclean-b2-additive.png). On ended, playNext fires immediately (player.js:556-558), with no 'up next' moment. A single video ends on 'Ended · Enter to play' plus 'End of list.' (end-x1-ended-additive.png).
findings.recommendation: Show a 5s 'Up next' card in the bottom band ('Down: play now · Left: cancel') with the next title and a countdown ring. Default Repeat to Off for phone pushes. When the list ends, show 'Finished · pinch to replay · Left to exit' and hide the chrome after 10s to save battery.

findings.title: Progress is saved 2.5 times a second while playing
findings.evidence: The tick (player.js:332-343) calls updateChrome every 400ms. While playing, updateChrome calls progressSave (app.js:1046), which does markSet (a JSON parse and stringify of up to 60 marks plus setItem), writes PROGRESS_KEY with up to 20 queue rows, and updates the Continue DOM. That is about 5 synchronous storage operations per tick on a battery-limited device.
findings.recommendation: Save at most every 5s, and also on pause, ended, exit and visibilitychange. The tick can drop to 1s once playing (keep 250ms only while the seek toast is showing).

audits.area: Runtime performance, battery and robustness on the glasses' Android WebView
audits.summary: The HUD itself is light. Home has 143 elements and a 20-result search 288. JS heap stays at 1-2.6 MB. 15 player open/close cycles leaked nothing (nodes 360 to 365, listeners 36 to 37). No JS errors on any screen, no filters or blur, and per-tick script cost is about 0.25 ms even at 4x CPU throttle. The real problems are in the timing and network layer around it: every pairing poll is fire-and-forget (no timeout, no in-flight guard, no ordering check), it polls every 2 s forever, the page never updates itself, and a third-party font stylesheet can blank the whole app. Several of these map directly onto the three known live problems: missed pushes, a stale page that lives for days, and false "Enter to play" gates. Two confirmed bugs stand out. Player.js reads window.GlassPrefs and window.GlassSound, which are undefined, so Speed, Captions, Sound Off and the battery-saving "Audio only" never take effect. And the production proxy route takes 61-65 s to fail, so every video not pushed with a file wastes 12 s behind a misleading "Enter to play". The single biggest opportunity is to rebuild pollPair into a guarded, timed-out, visibility-aware loop that also carries a deployment id. That one change makes pushes reliable, shows the wearer when the phone link is dead, cuts idle traffic by about two thirds, and gives the glasses self-update.

findings.title: Player ignores Speed, Captions, Sound Off and Audio-only (battery saver does nothing)
findings.evidence: prefs.js:1 and sound.js:1 declare `const GlassPrefs` / `const GlassSound` at top level. That creates global lexical bindings, not window properties. player.js:62 `window.GlassSound` and player.js:66 `window.GlassPrefs` are therefore undefined. Measured in the harness: typeof window.GlassPrefs === 'undefined' and typeof GlassPrefs === 'object'. During playback I set speed 1.5, Sound Off and Audio only, then called renderSettings(). 1.5 s later the video still had playbackRate=1 and muted=false, and #yt-wrap had no 'audio-only' class. GlassSound.setEnabled(false) mutes for an instant, then applyAll()/applySound() unmutes, because soundOn() is always true. Screenshot apl-player-audioonly.png shows full video in audio-only mode. Average picture level was 32.6% vs 32.7% in video mode, with 21% of pixels above 200 luminance in both.
findings.recommendation: In player.js use the lexical names: `const prefs = () => (typeof GlassPrefs !== 'undefined' ? GlassPrefs : null)` and `soundOn = () => !(typeof GlassSound !== 'undefined' && !GlassSound.enabled())`. Or add `window.GlassPrefs = GlassPrefs` / `window.GlassSound = GlassSound` at the end of prefs.js and sound.js. Then make Audio only actually save power. Hide #yt-slot with display:none rather than visibility:hidden. Show the poster small and dim (e.g. 160x90 at opacity .35, bottom-left) instead of a full-bright 600x338 image. Ideally ask the phone for an audio-only itag so nothing is decoded. Expected: a lit area of roughly 3-5% instead of about 50% during audio-only listening, plus Sound Off and Speed finally honoured.

findings.title: Pairing poll has no timeout, no in-flight guard and no ordering check: stalls are invisible and late responses replay old pushes
findings.evidence: app.js:1487 runs `setInterval(pollPair, 2000)`. app.js:1514 calls fetch with no AbortController (none of the 12 fetches in app.js has a timeout). app.js:1560 accepts any `d.destSeq !== pairLastSeq`. I simulated a 30 s stall: 10 polls stacked in flight at 20 s (15 by recovery, all resolving in a burst). Meanwhile the HUD still read 'Code TESTQA · listening', pairState 'paired', and showed no status (stall-during-stall.png), so a push sent during the stall is silently missed, which is known problem 1. I also delayed one poll response by 3.5 s. Push B (NASA) applied at 13.9 s, the late seq-1 response re-applied push A (Veritasium) at 17.4 s, then the next poll re-applied B at 18.4 s. With video pushes, the old video would cut in and the new one restart. Production is HTTP/2, so out-of-order responses are possible; production poll latency measured 220-280 ms, with an 850 ms cold start.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite pollPair as a self-scheduling loop instead of setInterval. Skip the tick if a poll is busy. Wrap the fetch in an AbortController with a 6 s timeout, then use setTimeout for the next poll. Only act on `d.destSeq > pairLastSeq` (monotonic), and persist pairLastSeq in localStorage so a reload cannot replay the last push. Whether the server keeps dest after ack is unverified: the SQL lives in Berth. Track lastPollOkAt. If it is older than 10 s, show 'Phone link lost · retrying' on the From iPhone row and as a one-line status in the player. Include pollAgeS and in-flight count in every hudNote so server logs can tell 'glasses never heard it' from 'glasses skipped it'.

findings.title: No self-update: deployed HUD changes never reach a page kept alive for days, and the build stamp cannot show it
findings.evidence: There is no visibilitychange, pageshow or location.reload anywhere in app.js or player.js. window.GLASSTUBE_BUILD = '1.25' (index.html:70) was last changed in e915109 (2026-09-14), yet app.js changed on 2026-10-08 (a379028, app.js?v=36). Diagnostics therefore shows 'v1.25' for both old and new code. Cache headers themselves are fine: '/' is no-store, and JS/CSS are 'public, max-age=0, must-revalidate' with manual ?v= busters, so a plain reload does fetch fresh code. Production now byte-matches the repo for index.html, app.js, player.js and styles.css.
findings.recommendation: Piggyback on the poll that already runs every 2 s. In api/pair.js GET, add `build: process.env.VERCEL_DEPLOYMENT_ID || process.env.VERCEL_URL` to the JSON. That value changes on every deploy, with no manual bump. In pollPair, store the first build seen as bootBuild. When a later poll reports a different build, set wantReload.
