Reload when current !== 'player' (or the player is paused, ended or errored) and there has been no keypress for 20 s: call progressSave() then location.reload(). To prevent reload loops, keep `glasstube.reloadedFor = build` in localStorage and skip if it is already equal. Show bootBuild in Diagnostics in place of the hand-typed 1.25. Expected: every deploy reaches the glasses within about a minute of the wearer going idle.

findings.title: Google Fonts stylesheet is render-blocking and also blocks app.js: a slow or blocked fonts.googleapis.com means a blank HUD with no pairing
findings.evidence: index.html:24 loads `<link rel=stylesheet href=https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Roboto...>` in head. Scripts at the end of body wait for pending stylesheets, so app.js (pairing poll, push handling, keys) cannot run until it resolves. Measured: normal warm load gives first paint at 116 ms. A 6 s fonts delay gives first paint and DOMContentLoaded at 6.65 s and splash-out at 7.55 s. A hanging fonts request (my stub held it 120 s) gave first paint at 121.8 s: the page was transparent on the glasses and polling never started. A fast failure (blocked) is harmless, with first paint at 1.1-1.8 s. Fonts cost 2 third-party origins plus a 37 KB woff2 on each daily cold load.
findings.recommendation: Self-host the font. Copy the latin Roboto variable woff2 (the same 37 KB file Google serves) to /fonts/roboto-latin.woff2 and serve it with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` in vercel.json. Declare it in styles.css: `@font-face{font-family:Roboto;src:local('Roboto'),url(/fonts/roboto-latin.woff2) format('woff2');font-weight:400 700;font-display:swap}` and add `<link rel=preload as=font type=font/woff2 crossorigin href=/fonts/roboto-latin.woff2>`. Delete the two preconnects and the googleapis link. Expected: no third-party dependency on the launch path, removing a 300-700 ms TLS handshake to two Google origins on cold start and the blank-screen, no-polling failure mode.

findings.title: Proxy route takes 61-65 s to fail in production: every non-pushed video wastes 12 s and each prefetch keeps a function busy for about a minute
findings.evidence: Measured against production for 8WSyoITbP-c: GET /api/watch returned 404 after 64.8 s, ?probe=1 answered after 61.5 s with every client 403 (ANDROID, ANDROID_VR, IOS), and the prefetch HEAD for dQw4w9WgXcQ returned 404 after 65.2 s. Videos without a phone file (Search, Channels, Recents, Playlists, Continue, which strips u at app.js:380-385, and Library) get the chain proxy>embed>go, and route memory never promotes past it when only 'file' ever worked. In the harness tour, the proxy sat on 'Enter to play' (tour-player.png) until the 12 s stall timer (app.js:874) moved to embed. prefetchNext (app.js:881-890) fires a HEAD /api/watch for the next item after every successful load, costing about 65 s of server time each for nothing today.
findings.recommendation: Server: wrap resolve() in api/watch.js in a 6-8 s overall timeout and cache negative results per id for 10 min, so failures return in under 1 s. Client: for the proxy route, call tryNextWay if `loadedmetadata` has not fired within 6 s, instead of waiting for the generic 12 s stall. Alternatively, run `/api/watch?probe=1` with a 5 s AbortController before mounting the <video>. Once the server is known to be blocked, demote proxy behind embed/go for the session. Remove prefetchNext, or only run it after a proxy load actually succeeded. Expected: non-pushed videos reach a working route or a clear error about 6-10 s sooner.

findings.title: 'Enter to play' gate is chosen by a 3.2 s timer, not by an autoplay rejection, and each track creates a fresh (re-locked) <video>
findings.evidence: app.js:851-862 sets needGesture whenever the state at 3.2 s is not playing, paused or error. A <video> still fetching has readyState<2, so state() returns -1 (player.js:617-624) and the gate shows. Reproduced with autoplay allowed and a local source with a 5 s first byte: at 3.2 s the gate read 'Enter to play' (slowsrc-gate-at-3s.png), and at about 5 s the video started by itself (gate gone, playing=true). tryPlay swallows the play() promise rejection (player.js:207), so the HUD never knows whether autoplay was really blocked. mountVideo (player.js:532-536) wipes the slot and creates a new <video> for every route attempt and every track. Under Android WebView's default mediaPlaybackRequiresUserGesture, the gesture unlock is per media element, so each new element starts locked again. This is a likely contributor to known problem 3, to be confirmed on device.
findings.recommendation: (1) In tryPlay, record the rejection: `p.catch(e => { if (e && e.name === 'NotAllowedError') autoplayBlocked = true; })`. Show the gate only when autoplayBlocked is set. Otherwise show 'Loading...' or 'Buffering', with readyState and buffered seconds in the hudNote check3s payload. (2) Keep one persistent <video id=yt-host> for the file and proxy routes and swap src (`v.src = url; v.load()`) instead of recreating it. (3) On the first trusted keydown anywhere in the HUD, call `v.muted = true; v.play().catch(()=>{}); v.pause()` once to unlock that element. Later phone pushes can then autoplay without a pinch. Verify on the glasses by adding a `playRejected` field to check3s.

findings.title: Pairing poll runs every 2 s forever, plus a 'touch' POST every 16 s, regardless of screen or visibility
findings.evidence: Idle-home measurement over 30 s: 15 GET /api/pair and 2 POST touch (app.js:1544, `pairPolls % 8` at 2 s means every 16 s). The same rate continues during playback (play-20s run: 10 polls and 1 touch in 20 s). That is about 2,025 requests per hour, or about 48,600 per day for a HUD left open. The glasses keep the page for days. Each request is a Vercel function plus a Berth RPC on the shared Postgres VM, taking 220-280 ms each in production. There is no visibilitychange handling anywhere, so radio wakeups every 2 s stop the WiFi link from reaching power save. The link token is valid for a year, so a touch every 16 s is far more than needed.
findings.recommendation: Use adaptive cadence in the new poll loop. Poll every 2 s while on the From iPhone screen or within 3 minutes of any key or push. Otherwise poll every 5 s while visible. Stop on `document.visibilityState === 'hidden'`, and poll immediately on visible, focus or the first keydown. Touch at most every 10 minutes, or drop it if the poll already refreshes last-seen. Expected: about 720 requests per hour when visible and idle (down 64%), about 0 when hidden, and push latency still about 1 s while the wearer is active.

findings.title: 400 ms player tick writes localStorage 3 times per tick and keeps running while paused or errored
findings.evidence: player.js:332-342 runs setInterval(400) with holdFocus() and onChange('tick'), which calls updateChrome(). When playing, updateChrome calls rememberRoute() and progressSave() every time (app.js:1045-1046). progressSave runs markSet (parse, sort and stringify of up to 60 marks), writes PROGRESS_KEY with up to 20 queue rows, and calls renderContinue. Measured: 149 localStorage writes in 20 s (7.3/s). With a 20-video queue, it wrote 241 KB in 30 s, about 29 MB per hour, for state that changes once a second. Chromium rate-limits localStorage commits (about 60 per hour and roughly 10 MB per hour per origin), so this volume buys nothing and can delay the real commit. The tick also continues during pause and blocked states: 2.5 wakeups per second for as long as the player screen is up. Per-call cost at 4x throttle is small (updateChrome 0.24 ms, progressSave 0.29 ms); the problem is frequency. 50 layouts per 20 s come from width changes on #player-fill and #player-buffer.
findings.recommendation: For the file and proxy routes, drive the chrome from media events (timeupdate, playing, pause, waiting, progress, error, ended). Keep a 1 s interval only for the embed/go iframes, and only while not paused. Stop the interval on pause, ended or error. Replace holdFocus polling with window 'blur' and document 'focusin' listeners. Save progress every 10 s while playing, and on pause, ended, back, visibilitychange hidden and pagehide. Call rememberRoute only when the route changes. Animate the bar with transform: scaleX to avoid layout. Expected: localStorage writes from about 7/s to about 0.1/s, and timer wakeups from 2.5/s to 1/s while playing and 0 while paused.

findings.title: Launch loads code and images nothing uses: YouTube iframe_api, an icon preload, and seven icon links
findings.evidence: app.js:1874 calls Player.preload(), which runs ensureApi() and injects https://www.youtube.com/iframe_api plus www-widgetapi.js on every launch (12-13 KB brotli, a new origin with DNS and TLS, 450-720 ms in the waterfall). Nothing uses it: `yt` is never assigned a YT.Player anywhere in player.js, and embed.html loads its own iframe_api inside its frame. index.html:19 preloads /icon-192.png (19 KB) at high priority, competing with the CSS and JS; Chrome warned 'preloaded using link preload but not used within a few seconds'. index.html:9-17 declares 7 icon links. Headless Chrome fetched favicon.png twice, favicon.ico (44 KB) and icon-512 (69 KB) on load.
findings.recommendation: Delete the Player.preload() call, and ensureApi/preload from player.js. Remove the icon-192 preload. Keep one 192 px PNG icon plus the manifest, and drop favicon.ico and the 512 link from the HUD head (the launcher reads the manifest). Expected: one fewer third-party origin and about 30 KB less on the launch critical path, and no YouTube script executing in the HUD document.

findings.title: Splash holds a fixed 900 ms plus a 600 ms fade, keyed to an element that no longer exists
findings.evidence: app.js:1890-1897 looks up `.splash-icon`, which does not exist (the splash uses a CSS .yt-mark), so it always falls through to setTimeout(hideSplash, 900). Warm reload: DOMContentLoaded at 88 ms, first paint at 116 ms, splash-out at 1011 ms, so about 900 ms of pure waiting on every launch, followed by a 600 ms opacity transition (styles.css:78).
findings.recommendation: Call hideSplash() at the end of init, or after the first poll answers, capped at 300 ms. Remove the splash-icon code and shorten the fade to 200 ms. Since the home header shows the same mark, the splash could also go entirely. Expected: interactive about 0.9 s sooner on every launch or reload, which matters more once self-update reloads the page.

findings.title: Thumbnails: loading=lazy does nothing in a 600 px list, and some paths use hqdefault
findings.evidence: A NASA search (limit=20) loaded 19 of 20 thumbnails right away (206 KB from i.ytimg.com) while about 5 rows are visible. Chrome's lazy-load distance threshold is larger than the whole list. The channel feed loads 6 thumbnails (50 KB). Sizes measured for the same videos: default.jpg about 2.8 KB (120x90), mqdefault about 11.5 KB (320x180), hqdefault about 19 KB (480x360). The slot is 128x72, so default.jpg with object-fit:cover crops its letterbox and is nearly native. recentsAdd (app.js:142), playlistRemember (app.js:487) and the poster fallback (player.js:610) use hqdefault.
findings.recommendation: Use default.jpg (or mqdefault) for list rows, and set src only for rows within about 2 screens of focus: an IntersectionObserver with root #list-items and rootMargin '200px', or assign src in reveal(). Use mqdefault instead of hqdefault for the stored fallbacks. Expected: thumbnail bytes per search drop by 70-85% (206 KB to about 30-60 KB), with fewer image decodes while swiping.

findings.title: Screenshot harness leaks fake glasses diagnostics into production logs
findings.evidence: shot.mjs intercepts only POST /api/watch. The HUD's diagSend posts to /api/diag (app.js:714), which the harness forwards to production, where vercel.json rewrites it to /api/watch. `vercel logs --since 6h` showed 16 POST /api/diag rows logged as '[glasstube-diag] {kind:push|fail, ua: ...Greatwhite...}' from origin http://127.0.0.1:55646-58593, i.e. audit runs. These look like real glasses events and pollute the evidence being used to debug the missed-push problem.
findings.recommendation: In shot.mjs, intercept `/api/diag` POSTs the same way as /api/watch (print them as [hud-report]). When reading production logs for known problem 1, discard entries whose origin starts with http://127.0.0.1.

research.platform:
HARDWARE (official, as Meta stated it and the press reported it): one full-colour 600x600 panel in the RIGHT lens, 20 deg field of view, 42 pixels per degree, auto brightness from 30 to 5,000 nits, panel at 90 Hz but content updates at 30 Hz. Wi-Fi 6 and Bluetooth 5.3. Sources: roadtovr.com/meta-ray-ban-smart-glasses-display-price-release-date-specs and gsmarena.

RUNTIME (official): a Chromium WebView on Android 14 (UA "Greatwhite", Chrome 151, observed). It needs glasses firmware v125+ and Meta AI app v272+. HTTPS only. Device pixel ratio is 1. Meta's toolkit gives this measurement profile (official, facebook/meta-wearables-webapp AGENTS.md "device envelope"): about 500 Kbps down (1 KB is about 16 ms), about 150 ms round trip, CPU about 12x slower than a laptop core, 30 Hz panel (33 ms frame budget). The targets that go with it: first paint under 1 s, usable under 5 s, first load under 300 KB, warm launch under 2 s with 0 bytes, fewer than 15 requests, heap under 128 MB. A Meta study measured startup at 650 ms native vs 3,900 ms web.

DISPLAY (official): additive light. #000 means no light, so the world shows through. Meta's guidance is a black canvas with bounded dark surfaces, not bright full-screen fills. Check readability over both bright and dark scenes, and never show state by colour alone. The docs say to treat 600x600 as a validation target and size from the viewport. Meta's custom-UI contract still accepts a fixed 600x600 root.

Values from @wearables-ui-toolkit/mrbd 129.23.0 styles.css (official):
- Typography: Noto Sans. numeral1 80/80, numeral2 64, display1 64/84, heading1 40/48 bold, heading2 36/44 bold, body1 32/40, body2 28/36, label and meta1 24/32, meta2 22/28, meta3 18/24 (the smallest style).
- Spacing: 2, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24 (page inset), 32, 40, 48, 56, 64 px.
- Metrics: system-bar inset at the top 24 px, header area 64 px, ListItem at least 120 px tall, Button 88 px, chip 44 px, fading edges 32 / 64 / 88 / 100 px.
- Colours: window #000, text #fff, secondary #cfd3d9 (with a lighten blend), placeholder #aaafb9, surfaces #27282d and #30333a, border #ffffff40, accent #2694fe, positive #26a756, negative #ff5668, warning #c58600.

INPUT (official): the temple touchpad and the Neural Band deliver only keydown ArrowUp, ArrowDown, ArrowLeft, ArrowRight and Enter. There is no pointer, touch or keyboard. Chromium spatial navigation is on by default. Pinch-drag pointer events are opt-in through body{touch-action:none} in the first stylesheet. The toolkit's own timings: long press 500 ms, minimum pressed feedback 120 ms, arrows under 140 ms apart count as fast scroll.

BACK (official): since firmware v125.1, the middle-finger + thumb tap calls history.back() when history has an entry. Your page sees that as popstate, never as a key. With no history left it opens the native overlay / universal Web App menu (Restart, Resume, Permissions), and a second Back exits. pushState is capped at 5 entries including the root, and the root should be seeded with replaceState. Older glasses-app notes say the OS "never forwards" back; that was true before v125.1 or when the history stack is empty.

TEXT INPUT (official): input type=text or search, textarea and contenteditable open the system composer (handwriting, dictation, keyboard) on focus plus pinch. Firmware v127+ is needed for the composer and v129+ for the on-screen keyboard. It cannot type ' " _ [ ]. Read the text from input/change events. Programmatic .focus() does not open it.

LIFECYCLE (official plus observed):
- Official: if a new deploy behaves like the old build, use Restart in the universal menu. A new service worker waits until the old pages close.
- Official: localStorage and sessionStorage hold 5 MB each and can be wiped by app removal, device reset or storage pressure. Service workers and the Cache API work for an offline shell.
- Observed (IronMath 2a06d7b): an open page keeps its loaded bundle for days.
- Observed (GlassNav f845e40) and community (audiojoe4444/GlassTube): the glasses lose browser storage between launches, and firmware updates can wipe it.

ICONS (official, page dated 2026-09-22): the App Manager reads only /.well-known/meta-wearables-manifest.json, relative to the launch URL's directory. It needs version 1, a name, appearance.theme_color and/or icon_background.colors, and a monochrome transparent icon designed for a 64x64 area. PNG, WebP and SVG are allowed. The manifest must be 64 KiB or less, the icon 2 MiB or less (SVG 512 KiB or less, raster 4096 px or less), served as application/json; charset=utf-8. The legacy dialog uses PNG favicons, which must be larger than 52x52; SVG favicons are not supported. The QR install link is fb-viewapp://web_app_deep_link?appName=..&appUrl=..; navigator.install() also works.

MEDIA: no official Web Apps document covers video or autoplay (I searched both the docs and Meta's docs MCP server). speechSynthesis is official: one en-US voice, volume ignored, plays through the glasses speaker, and errors include audio-busy. The Display Access rule "video at most 400 px per side and 70,000 px" applies to phone-rendered video over Bluetooth, NOT to web apps. Inferred from Chrome policy: muted autoplay is allowed, sound needs user activation, and a pinch keydown grants activation that stays for the life of the page.

HOW TO TEST:
- Meta Ray-Ban Display Simulator Chrome extension (additive blend, scenes, D-pad, QA checklist, View on Glasses QR).
- Record Display from the Meta AI app (Devices > Record Display) or from the glasses settings.
- Docs MCP server at https://mcp.developer.meta.com/wearables (tool search_webapps_docs). It needs no auth and I queried it with curl.

Research files are under /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mike/d0c887a3-23b0-4c19-8596-7e911651ee39/scratchpad/hudtools/audit/platform/ (web/*.txt, pkg/, repos/, home-*-additive.png).

rules.rule: Self-update a stale HUD. At deploy, stamp every /api/pair response with the build (for example d.v='1.26'). When d.v !== window.GLASSTUBE_BUILD, call location.replace with ?rv=<d.v> added. Do it at most once per build: skip if the URL already has rv=d.v. Never reload while current==='player'; defer until playback stops or the HUD is idle on home.
rules.why: The glasses keep the old page in memory for days, so fixes never arrive (GlassTube live problem 2). The rv marker stops a reload loop that would drain the battery.

rules.rule: Teach the official manual refresh in Help and Diagnostics: 'Old version? Middle-finger tap on the home screen, then Restart.' Also show the build stamp (vX.Y) big for about 3 s at launch, then fade it out.
rules.why: Meta's documented fix for a deploy that behaves like the old build is Restart in the universal Web App menu. Cook fades its v11 stamp after launch so Mike can see on the lens that the new build loaded.
rules.source: https://wearables.developer.meta.com/docs/develop/webapps/troubleshoot/ and /test/ (universal menu: Restart, Resume, Permissions); /Users/mike/Documents/Cook commit 7ff7b02

rules.rule: Handle the page lifecycle. On visibilitychange to visible and on pageshow: poll /api/pair right away (do not wait for the 2 s interval), re-run the version check, and call navigator.serviceWorker registration.update() if a worker exists. On hidden: clear the poll interval, or back it off to 10 s or more. Restart at 2 s when visible again. GlassTube currently has no visibilitychange or pageshow handler.
rules.why: Glasses web apps are resumed, not navigated to. Without this the HUD can sit on a stale poll schedule or a stale build after the display wakes. The toolkit says to close polling when hidden.
rules.source: Cook/glasses/app.js:1608; IronMath/glasses/app.v11.js (pageshow + visibilitychange restart polling); glassflow/js/hud.js:665; facebook/meta-wearables-webapp plugins/.../docs/offline-caching.md (update() on launch and when the page returns to the foreground)

rules.rule: Make pairing outlive storage wipes. Read the pairing in this order: launch URL (?pair=CODE or a link token in the Meta AI web-app URL), then localStorage, then a 1-year cookie. Write it to all three. Show the pinnable URL on the From iPhone screen. GlassTube today keeps glasstube.pair and glasstube.link in localStorage only.
rules.why: The glasses lose browser storage between launches. GlassTube would then mint a new code while the phone keeps pushing to the old pairing, which is exactly 'Playing on your glasses' with nothing happening (live problem 1). The launcher URL is the only store that survives a wipe.
rules.source: /Users/mike/Documents/glassnav commit f845e40; glassboard README (?code=48CA9F baked into the launch URL); community audiojoe4444/GlassTube README ('Glasses software updates can wipe a web app's saved data')

rules.rule: Make delivery honest. Let the phone say 'Playing on your glasses' only after the HUD acks: the HUD POSTs {ev:'playing', destSeq} on the video's 'playing' event, or {ev:'gate'} if it is waiting for a pinch. Otherwise the phone shows 'Sent. Glasses last checked in Ns ago' from lastSeen, and warns when that is over 10 s.
rules.why: A push 'succeeds' whenever the pairing row exists, even with no glasses listening. GlassNav and GlassFlow had to add liveness and an echo so the phone stopped claiming delivery.

rules.rule: Use browser history for Back. At boot call history.replaceState({s:'home'},''). Push one entry per drill-down level (home > list > video or player), at most 4 pushes, because the cap is 5 entries including the root. Render screens from popstate event.state. Never pushState inside the popstate handler. At home, let Back fall through to the native menu.
rules.why: Since firmware v125.1 the Neural Band's middle-finger + thumb tap calls history.back() when history exists. That gives GlassTube a real one-gesture Back instead of spending ArrowLeft on it.
rules.source: https://wearables.developer.meta.com/docs/develop/webapps/build/input-and-navigation/ ; github.com/facebook/meta-wearables-webapp issue #12 (a Meta contributor confirms v125.1)

rules.rule: Once system Back works, give ArrowLeft in the player a playback job (seek -10 s, or show controls) and route every Back through one goBack() that calls history.back(). On list screens Left may stay as a Back alias, but it must call the same history path.
rules.why: Today a stray left swipe exits the video. Meta says any on-screen Back must call the same history action, not keep separate navigation state.

rules.rule: Keep calling preventDefault() on every arrow key and Enter you handle (GlassTube's capture-phase listener already does). Never call el.click() for Enter without preventing the default Enter action.
rules.why: Chromium WebView spatial navigation is on by default. Without preventDefault, your focus move and the browser's both run, and Enter can activate a control twice.

rules.rule: On keydown Enter, ignore events with e.repeat === true.
rules.why: Enter auto-repeat is the band still holding the pinch, not new pinches. Without this, toggles flip back and forth and a play/pause pinch can fire several times.

rules.rule: Ignore Enter for 320 ms after any arrow swipe when it arrives as a keydown/keyup pair, and for 520 ms when it arrives as an atomic click or select.
rules.why: A flick ends with the wrist settling, and the band often reports that as a pinch. In GlassTube that plays whatever row the swipe just landed on.

rules.rule: Run all input through one arbiter. Drop the same gesture repeated within 130 ms (one physical gesture fanned out as key + synthetic click + wrist event). Treat a different gesture within 240 ms of a commit as a side effect. Treat the same arrow within 140 ms as one swipe; for long lists, accelerate instead of dropping.
rules.why: One physical gesture reaches the page from several sources at once. Meta's toolkit also uses 140 ms as its fast-scroll threshold.
rules.source: Cook/glasses/app.js (DUP_MS 130, CROSS_MS 240); glassflow/js/input.js and glassboard/js/input.js emit() 140 ms; @wearables-ui-toolkit/foundation Interactions.d.ts FAST_SCROLL_THRESHOLD_MS 140

rules.rule: Never map unknown key codes to a direction. Resolve e.key, then e.code, then keyCode (37-40, 13), then Android keycodes (19-23, 66). Otherwise ignore the event.
rules.why: A guessed fallback direction made one swipe go right and the next go left, so the HUD looked dead.

rules.rule: Make playback swipe-proof. While a video plays, swipes only show controls or seek; skipping to the next or previous video, or leaving the player, needs a pinch on a visible control or system Back. Swallow wheel events. GlassTube now skips to the next video on a bare ArrowDown.
rules.why: A bump against the band must not drop the video. Cook treats up/down as wrist-tilt noise and wheel as a tilt sensor. GlassNav made its walking screens swipe-proof for the same reason.
rules.source: Cook/glasses/app.js onKeyDown ('Up and down are wrist tilt on this band') and the wheel swallow; glassnav commit 702955e

rules.rule: Long press only for non-essential shortcuts: 500 ms threshold (Meta toolkit), or 680 ms with a progress meter that appears after 180 ms (Cook). Presses under 45 ms are noise, a double pinch is two within 550 ms, and a press with no release after 2,100 ms counts as released.
rules.why: Holds are slow, ambiguous and undiscoverable. These numbers are tuned on the band.
rules.source: @wearables-ui-toolkit/foundation dist/base/Interactions.d.ts LONG_PRESS_TIMEOUT 500, QUICK_PRESS_RELEASE_DELAY 120; Cook/glasses/app.js HOLD_MS 680, HOLD_ARM_MS 180, TAP_MIN_MS 45, DOUBLE_MS 550, STUCK_MS 2100

rules.rule: For search, put a native <input type="search"> first. A pinch on it opens the system composer (dictation, handwriting, keyboard); read the text from 'input' and 'change'. Keep the letter grid as a fallback. Strip ' " _ [ ] from required inputs, since the composer cannot type them.
rules.why: The grid needs many swipes per letter; dictation is one gesture. The composer needs firmware v127+ (on-screen keyboard v129+) and opens only on focus plus activation, never from programmatic .focus().
rules.source: https://wearables.developer.meta.com/docs/develop/webapps/build/input-and-navigation/ (Text input); facebook/meta-wearables-webapp AGENTS.md ('Do not build a custom keyboard')

rules.rule: Write on-lens hints in gesture words: 'Pinch to play', 'Swipe left', 'Middle-finger tap to go back'. Never use 'Enter', 'Escape' or 'Backspace'.
rules.why: The glasses never send those key names, so the hints confused the wearer.

rules.rule: Type scale: no text under 18 px. Metadata 22 px, list labels 24 px, routine copy 28 px, primary titles 32-40 px bold, big numbers 64-80 px. GlassTube home rows are 18 px labels with 14 px subtitles, and settings and debug use 12-16 px: raise every one of them.
rules.why: These are Meta's own sizes on this 600 px, DPR 1 additive panel. Small or thin text breaks up over bright scenes, and the additive screenshot confirms the 14 px subtitles nearly vanish.

rules.rule: Text colours: #fff primary, #cfd3d9 secondary (with mix-blend-mode: lighten), #aaafb9 for placeholder or disabled only. Nothing dimmer for text: drop GlassTube's #8d8d8d back hint. Status colours: #2694fe accent, #26a756 positive, #ff5668 error, #c58600 warning, always paired with an icon or word.
rules.why: Dim greys add almost no light, so they vanish against the world. Meta requires state to be shown by more than colour alone.

rules.rule: Separate content with bounded dark surfaces (#1C1E21 to #30333a, radius 16-24 px) on a #000 page, never with large light fills. Show focus with a bright 2-3 px stroke or glow plus content going from 80% opacity at idle to 100% when focused, not a light-grey full-width bar like GlassTube's current focused row.
rules.why: Large bright areas wash out the world and cost battery. Meta says to add bounded surfaces instead of painting a bright background.

rules.rule: Focus animation: about 475 ms on with cubic-bezier(0.6,0,0.4,1), 625 ms off, 100 ms press, at least 120 ms of visible press feedback. Animate transform and opacity only.
rules.why: These match the system feel. Other properties force layout work on a CPU about 12x slower than a laptop, with a 33 ms frame budget at 30 Hz.

rules.rule: Controls: list rows at least 88 px tall (Meta's ListItem is 120 px with a 74 px thumbnail), buttons 88 px, chips 44 px. That means about 4 rows per screen, not GlassTube's 7 rows at about 58 px.
rules.why: Bigger targets give larger text and fewer, clearer focus stops. They also give a scrolling list room to signal that more content follows.

rules.rule: Insets: 24 px left and right, at least 24 px clear at the top for the system bar, a 64 px header area. No control within 8 px of any edge. Put the main block (title, play gate, now-playing) in the middle third of the panel.
rules.why: System UI and the focus rubber-band clip edge controls, and the waveguide is sharpest in the centre.
rules.source: @wearables-ui-toolkit/mrbd (SYSTEM_BAR_INSET_TOP = 24, --uit-header-area-length 64px, --uit-spacing-large 24px); game docs display-guidelines.md (8 dp safe margin); glassnav commit 51d8209

rules.rule: Use only the 2/4/8/12/16/20/24/32/40/48/56/64 px spacing steps: 20 px between lines of a text stack, 32 px between sections.
rules.why: This is Meta's spacing scale, and it keeps rhythm consistent with system apps.

rules.rule: Overflow: one scroll owner per axis, with a 32-88 px fading edge as the 'more below' cue. Auto-shrink only as a last resort, and never below about 24 px for primary text. If text still does not fit, cut at a word boundary with an ellipsis rather than slicing through glyphs.
rules.why: Meta prefers intentional scrolling over 'shrinking everything until it becomes unreadable'. GlassFlow's fit stops at 0.62x and Cook's ladder goes 54, 46, 40, 34, 30, 26 then trims.

rules.rule: Drop the Google Fonts Roboto link (3 weights). Use a local stack instead: 'Noto Sans', system-ui, Roboto, sans-serif.
rules.why: On a link of about 500 Kbps with about 150 ms round trips, two extra origins plus font files cost 1-2 s at launch. Meta's guidance says no external font downloads, and its toolkit prefers an installed Noto Sans.
rules.source: meta-wearables-webapp game docs performance-guidelines.md ('No external font downloads'); facebook/meta-wearables-webapp AGENTS.md (device envelope); toolkit typography page

rules.rule: Keep the launch budget: shell under 300 KB, fewer than 15 requests, first paint under 1 s, warm launch under 2 s. Stop every interval (pair poll, sleep watch, player tick) when hidden or off-screen.
rules.why: Meta's device profile is about 500 Kbps down, about 150 ms round trip, a 12x slower CPU and a 30 Hz panel.

rules.rule: Ask the phone for 360p or lower (for example muxed itag 18, 640x360). Size the video at most 600 px wide, about 338 px tall for 16:9.
rules.why: The panel is 600x600 at DPR 1, so anything above 360p cannot be seen. At about 500 Kbps, higher bitrates only cause stalls.
rules.source: first principles from the 600x600 DPR 1 display and the official device envelope

rules.rule: Do not apply the 'video at most 400 px per side and 70,000 px' limit to GlassTube.
rules.why: That rule is for the Display Access SDK, where the phone renders and sends video over Bluetooth, not for web apps.

rules.rule: Autoplay: keep the muted start and unmute on the first pinch. If the gate is needed, make it one pinch with a 40 px 'Pinch to play' in the centre. Avoid reloading the page (self-update, Restart) between a pinch and a push, because a reload loses user activation and the next push hits the gate again.
rules.why: No Web Apps document covers <video> autoplay, so Chrome's policy applies: muted autoplay is allowed, sound needs activation, and activation stays for the page's lifetime once granted.
rules.source: glasstube/player.js (html5.muted first); Chrome autoplay and user-activation policy

rules.rule: If the YouTube iframe route is used, set tabindex=-1 and aria-hidden on the iframe. On window blur, refocus the HUD's current control after about 60 ms.
rules.why: The iframe takes focus, and then the band's arrow keys go into YouTube instead of the HUD.
rules.source: community github.com/audiojoe4444/GlassTube app.js (blur handler, iframe tabindex -1)

rules.rule: Audio: create any AudioContext only on the first pinch and suspend it when hidden. For spoken feedback, speechSynthesis uses the single en-US voice at system volume ('volume' is ignored); handle onerror 'audio-busy' and always show the same text on screen.
rules.why: These are the documented audio behaviours on the glasses.
rules.source: https://wearables.developer.meta.com/docs/develop/webapps/build/text-to-speech/ ; game docs audio.md (Autoplay unlock and battery)

rules.rule: Add https://glasstube.vercel.app/.well-known/meta-wearables-manifest.json: {"version":1,"name":"GlassTube","appearance":{"theme_color":"#FF0033","icon":{"src":"../icon-mono.png","type":"monochrome"}}}. The icon is a transparent single-colour play mark designed for a 64x64 area. Serve the manifest as application/json; charset=utf-8, 64 KiB or less; icon 2 MiB or less. Keep PNG favicons larger than 52 px for the legacy dialog, and make sure favicon.ico does not lead with a 16x16 entry.
rules.why: The App Manager reads only this manifest and never looks at favicons, so GlassTube gets the fallback icon today. A 16x16 entry first in favicon.ico made the launcher fall back.
rules.source: https://wearables.developer.meta.com/docs/develop/webapps/build/app-icons/ ; /troubleshoot/ (SVG favicons not supported, PNG larger than 52x52); glassnav commit d548afd

rules.rule: Install and sharing: the QR code must encode fb-viewapp://web_app_deep_link?appName=GlassTube&appUrl=https%3A%2F%2Fglasstube.vercel.app%2F%3Fpair%3D<code>, not a plain URL. Add <meta name="application-name" content="GlassTube"> for navigator.install().
rules.why: A plain-URL QR code is not recognised. Putting the pair code in appUrl also makes the pairing durable (see the pairing rule).

rules.rule: Keep <meta name="mrbd-web-app-capable" content="yes"> and the description. GlassTube's fixed 600x600 #stage is fine under Meta's custom-UI contract; still check that no element overflows 600 px wide, because the Simulator QA test flags it.
rules.why: The tag is required platform metadata, and a custom (non-toolkit) app's root may be exactly 600x600.

rules.rule: Keep the crash bar registered before any other script, and add a '?swreset=1' escape hatch before ever adding a service worker. If you do add one, serve navigations network-first with no-cache, use cache-first only for hashed assets, and register with updateViaCache:'none'.

research.lessonsFromSiblings:
IronMath (/Users/mike/Documents/IronMath/glasses/app.v11.js, commit 2a06d7b):
- Already solved stale builds. /api/hud stamps every response with its deployed version. On a mismatch the lens reloads with ?rv=<version>, once per version, so it can never loop. It also restarts polling on pageshow and visibilitychange.
- Input is one-dimensional on purpose: left/right moves along one strip of actions and pinch activates. Up/down only change view.
- GlassTube has no version check, no pageshow handler and no visibilitychange handler. This is the direct fix for live problem 2.

GlassNav (/Users/mike/Documents/glassnav):
- f845e40: the glasses lose browser storage between launches, which orphaned the phone. The pair code now falls back localStorage, then a 1-year cookie, then ?pair= in the launcher URL, which is the durable one.
- e33d8e2: the HUD starts listening at launch no matter what and renews a dead code. The phone only says delivered when the glasses polled recently (lastSeenSecs); before that it reported 'Sent' to a pairing nobody listened to.
- GlassTube keeps the pairing in localStorage only, so it still has the exact orphaned-pairing bug behind live problem 1.
- Other GlassNav lessons:
  - Walking screens are swipe-proof: a bump on the band does nothing, and only a pinch opens a menu (702955e).
  - Hints say 'pinch' and 'swipe left', never 'Enter' or 'Escape' (4282472).
  - The waveguide is sharpest in the centre, so the main block is centred with margin off the FOV edge (51d8209).
  - favicon.ico leading with a 16x16 entry made the launcher fall back; PNGs are cached for 1 h, so icons get a version bump (d548afd).
  - The crash bar is registered before every other script.
  - Splash: 1,400 ms, then a 700 ms fade.
  - Bounded retries: 3 attempts with an 8 s timeout each.

Cook (/Users/mike/Documents/Cook/glasses/app.js):
- The most tuned Neural Band input, all in one arbiter:
  - One physical gesture arrives as key + synthetic click + wrist event. Same gesture within 130 ms is a duplicate; a different gesture within 240 ms is a side effect.
  - A flick's wrist-settle reads as a select, so Enter is locked out for 320 ms after a swipe (520 ms for atomic clicks).
  - Enter e.repeat is the pinch still held, so it is ignored.
  - Hold 680 ms with a meter after 180 ms; taps under 45 ms are noise; double pinch within 550 ms; a press with no release by 2,100 ms is treated as released.
  - Up/down and wheel events are treated as wrist-tilt noise.
- Fixed-region grid with targeted textContent updates, never innerHTML per tick.
- Text fits with a ladder (54, 46, 40, 34, 30, 26 px), then trims at a word boundary.
- A version stamp shows on the lens and then fades.
- The lens refreshes on visibilitychange.
- GlassTube has none of the input timing guards: no post-swipe Enter lockout, no e.repeat check, no dedupe. In the player, a bare Down skips the video and a bare Left exits.

GlassFlow and GlassBoard (js/input.js, hud.js):
- One shared input resolver: e.key, then e.code, then keyCode, then Android keycodes. Same direction within 140 ms counts as one swipe, and unknown codes are never guessed (a guessed fallback made the HUD look dead).
- GlassFlow:
  - Text auto-fits to a 0.62x floor.
  - Polling is hot, warm or cold by idle time and stops entirely while document.hidden.
  - It echoes what the lens shows back to the phone (sawTs) so the phone displays a confirmed state.
  - A versioned service worker gives an offline shell, with /api never cached.
  - Baked room code FLOW01.
- GlassBoard bakes ?code=48CA9F into the launch URL so the pairing never drifts.
- GlassTube has no echo of what is actually playing, no idle backoff and no hidden handling.

Type sizes:
- Siblings use 20-28 px body text and 46-168 px hero text (GlassFlow hero 46 / step 30 / body 23; Cook 24 body / 54 step / 168 clock; GlassBoard 92 name / 36 lines; IronMath 104-164 numerals).
- GlassTube uses 14-18 px for most of its text.

Back:
- Every sibling still treats ArrowLeft as back, because they predate firmware v125.1.
- The official platform now delivers the middle-finger Back as popstate when history exists (5-entry cap). None of the siblings uses this yet. The community GlassTube (audiojoe4444) does, with a pushState guard.

plan.vision: On the lens, GlassTube should feel like a quiet black window. Black is see-through on this display, so the world shows through everywhere except the few things that matter. Home is six large words, and a bright white ring marks the one a pinch will open. One status word says whether the iPhone is linked. Lists show about four big rows. Thumbnails stay dim until their row is focused, so the light the eye sees follows the user's attention. A playing video sits centred in the sharpest part of the lens, and nothing else is lit. Any swipe brings back a title band above and a thick progress line below for three seconds, then they fade. A bump on the band never skips or quits a video. Skipping takes Down and then a pinch on Next. Leaving takes two left swipes or the system Back gesture. Sending from the iPhone is a closed loop. The glasses show 'From your iPhone · <title>' and start playing with sound, because one swipe earlier in the session unlocks audio for the life of the page. The phone says 'Playing on your glasses' only after the glasses confirm it. Otherwise it says exactly what happened: not listening, waiting for a pinch, or could not play. A push that arrived while the glasses were away waits on Home as 'Missed from iPhone'. Search starts with dictation, offers suggestions after two letters, and keeps recent searches one swipe up. Every deploy reaches the glasses by itself the next time they sit idle on Home, and a version stamp shows briefly at launch so Mike can see it landed.
plan.designSystem:
CANVAS: fixed 600x600 #stage at DPR 1. Page background is #000, which shows as transparent on the lens. Font stack: 'Noto Sans', Roboto, system-ui, sans-serif. No web-font download. Every time or count uses font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums.

ZONES (y in px):
- 0-24: clear for the system bar.
- 24-88: header, 64px tall. 36x26 red play mark plus a 32px title on the left. Link chip on the right, plus a build chip that shows at launch.
- 88-552: content. One scroll owner, .screen-body.
- 500-548: toast lane, anchored to the bottom, above the footer.
- 556-580: footer hint, not focusable ('◀ Back').
- Side inset is 24px everywhere, so content runs x 24-576. Nothing focusable sits within 8px of any edge.
- Hero blocks (pair code, play gate, final error, 'Updated') are centred in the middle third, y 200-400.
- Player: top band y 24-120. Video 600x338 at y 131-469. HTML5 routes use a 600x600 box with object-fit: contain, so a 9:16 video gets 338x600. Bottom band y 480-576.

COLOUR TOKENS (on :root):
- --bg #000000
- --t1 #ffffff: titles, focused labels, focus ring.
- --t2 #cfd3d9: labels at rest and secondary text, about 80% brightness.
- --t3 #aaafb9: hints and disabled text only, never under 18px.
- --accent #ff3d3d: brand mark, the single Play-all fill, the Search key outline, the progress knob. Never text, never focus.
- --ok #4ff08f, --warn #ffc24a, --err #ff7a70: always paired with a glyph (✓ ! ✗) and a word, never colour alone.
- --hair rgba(255,255,255,.28): idle outlines of keys and chips.
- --track rgba(255,255,255,.22) and --buffer rgba(255,255,255,.45): progress bar.
- --surface #1c1e21: bounded backing for the player menu only. Never the only cue.

BANNED:
- Text darker than #aaafb9.
- Dark text on a light fill. On this display it reads as letters cut out of a bright slab.
- Any light fill larger than 48x48 other than video, thumbnails and the one red call to action.
- Black text-shadows and black scrims. They add no light, so they do nothing.
- The 14 hard-coded greys in today's styles.css (#212121, #272727, #303030, #3f3f3f, #8d8d8d, #c9c9c9 and so on).

COLOUR CONFLICTS RESOLVED:
- The accent stays YouTube red, not Meta blue #2694fe. Red is used only where its low brightness carries no meaning.
- Status colours are lighter than Meta's #26a756, #ff5668 and #c58600. They sit as text on pure black on an additive display, so they must give off enough light to read.

TYPE SCALE (size / line-height / weight, in px):
- Pair code: 64/72/800, letter-spacing 8.
- Screen title: 32/40/700.
- Player title: 28/34/700, clamped to 2 lines.
- Row label (home, settings, text rows, player menu): 28/36/600.
- Video title: 24/30/600, clamped to 2 lines with an ellipsis.
- Meta line and time: 22/28/500.
- Settings value: 24/30/700 in --t1.
- Toast: 24/30/600.
- Gate: 32/40/700.
- Keyboard keys: 28/600.
- Search field: 28/36/700.
- Chips: 22/600.
- Hint: 18/24/500. This is the smallest text anywhere.

Floor: 18px and weight 500. This resolves a conflict: the visual audit proposed a 16px floor, and Meta's toolkit uses an 18px floor with 22px metadata, 24px labels and 28px body. Meta's scale wins. It was set for exactly this 600px additive panel, and the audits' additive images show 14-16px secondary lines fading over bright scenes.

FOCUS (one style on every screen):
- .focusable{position:relative}
- .focusable::after{content:'';position:absolute;inset:0;border:3px solid #fff;border-radius:16px;opacity:0;transition:opacity 180ms cubic-bezier(.6,0,.4,1);pointer-events:none}
- .focusable:focus::after{opacity:1}
- The label goes from --t2 to --t1 on focus. Thumbnails go from opacity .55 to 1.
- No background fill, no red left bar, no animated box-shadow.
- Pinch feedback: .pressed{transform:scale(.97)} for 120ms.
- Keyboard cursor (.kb-on): the same ring plus transform: scale(1.06).

This resolves a conflict: the navigation audit proposed a red outline with an 8px left bar and dimming to .55, and the visual audit proposed a white ring. The white ring wins, because white is about 4x brighter than red on this panel. Dimming is kept only for thumbnails and resting labels.

ROWS AND TILES:
- Home row: 60px for a label only, 80px for a label plus a 22px status line. Radius 16, padding 0 20px, 4px gap, no separators. Six rows fit in y 88-552.
- Text list rows (Channels, Playlists, Library, Settings): 64px, or 84px with a second line.
- Settings value: right-aligned, 24/700 --t1, with ‹ › in --t3 when the row is focused.
- Video row: 112px. 160x90 thumbnail at radius 12, using mqdefault.jpg. 16px gap. Title 24/30 on two lines, meta 22 on one line. Four rows fit on a screen, matching Meta's ListItem guidance.
- Play all: the only filled button. 64px tall, radius 32, --accent background, 24/700 white text 'Play all · 20'. Focus ring offset 4px.
- Channel and playlist rows are plain text rows, not pills.
- Size conflict: Meta's ListItem is 88-120px tall. Video rows follow it at 112px. Text rows stay at 60-84px so Home fits on one screen without scrolling.

SEARCH SCREEN:
- Field: native <input type=search>, 52px tall, transparent, with a 2px --hair underline. Shows the end of the query, not the start. 2px white blinking caret.
- Chips row: 44px tall, radius 22, 1.5px --hair outline, 22px --t2 text.
- Grid: 10 columns of 52px keys (about 51.6px wide) with 4px gaps. Letters 28/600 --t2 inside 1.5px --hair outlines.
- Action row: Search | Delete | Clear | Back. The Search key has a 2px --accent outline and fills with --accent (white text) only while the cursor is on it.

PLAYER:
- The video is at full brightness while playing. It drops to opacity .35 under the gate, pause, menu or final error. Opacity is used, not filter, so the work stays on the compositor and the light really dims.
- Chrome bands fade in on load, on any key, on pause, on error, and when buffering lasts over 1s. They fade out 3s after playback resumes. With chrome hidden, only the video is lit.
- Bottom band: 6px bar (--track track, --buffer buffered, white fill drawn with transform: scaleX) with a 14px --accent knob. Time 22/600 on the left. 'Next: …' 22 --t2 on the right, with an ellipsis.
- Seek feedback: '+10s' at 28/800 inside the bottom band.
- Gate: a 64px ▶ glyph plus 'Pinch to play' at 32/700, inside a 3px white ring pill with no fill, centred at y 300.
- No text is ever drawn over the picture.

SPACING: use only 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48 and 64px. 20px between stacked text lines, 32px between sections.

OVERFLOW:
- One scroll owner per screen.
- Keep the focused row centred: scrollIntoView with block 'center', scroll-padding 24px.
- 32px black-to-transparent gradient overlays at the top and bottom of the scroll area, shown only when content continues past that edge.
- An 'n/N' counter at 22px --t3 to the right of list titles.
- Cut long text at a word boundary with an ellipsis. Never shrink primary text below 24px.

MOTION:
- Animate transform and opacity only.
- Focus ring: 180ms on, 240ms off, cubic-bezier(.6,0,.4,1). This is faster than Meta's 475/625ms because swipes arrive under 140ms apart and the panel content updates at 30 Hz.
- Press 120ms, toast 250ms, chrome 300ms.
- The spinner is the only animation that loops forever, and only while it is visible. The caret blinks only while Search is visible.
- No per-frame JavaScript. UI timers tick at most once a second.

COPY: gesture words and glyphs only, such as 'Pinch to play' and 'Swipe left to go back' with ▲▼◀▶. Never 'Enter', 'Escape' or 'Backspace'.

workPackages.title: Lifecycle foundation: guarded polling, self-update, lifecycle handlers, stop pairing loss
workPackages.goal: Every later fix reaches the glasses on its own. Polling is single-flight, times out and adapts to what the wearer is doing. The two ways the HUD silently drops its pairing are closed.
workPackages.changes:
Make all changes in app.js unless another file is named.

1. Build stamp, new file scripts/stamp.mjs:
- Compute an 8-hex sha256 for each of app.js, player.js, styles.css, prefs.js and sound.js. Rewrite every ?v= on the matching <script src> and <link href> in index.html to that file's hash.
- Compute GLASSTUBE_BUILD as an 8-hex sha256 over all per-file hashes, embed.html, and index.html with the build value and ?v= values blanked. Write it into index.html (window.GLASSTUBE_BUILD = '<hash>') and into a new api/_build.js (export const BUILD = '<hash>';). The underscore keeps api/_build.js from counting as a function, so the total stays at 12.
- The script must be idempotent.
- package.json scripts: "stamp": "node scripts/stamp.mjs" and "deploy": "node scripts/stamp.mjs && vercel --prod".

2. api/pair.js:
- Import BUILD and add build: BUILD to every GET response, including { ok: false } responses.
- noteAgent: log req.query.b, i and who. Rate-limit the log per key with a Map from key to last-logged time, not one global timer.

3. Poll loop:
- Replace setInterval(pollPair, PAIR_POLL_MS) with a setTimeout chain: schedulePoll(ms), pollNow() and a pollBusy flag, so only one request is ever in flight. Wrap each fetch in an AbortController with an 8s timeout.
- Cadence pollDelay():
  - document.hidden: 15000ms. Hidden still polls, because whether the glasses report hidden truthfully is unverified.
  - current === 'phone', or Date.now() - lastActiveAt < 180000: 2000ms.
  - Otherwise: 5000ms.
  - lastActiveAt updates at boot, on visible, on any keydown and when a push is applied.
- On a network or HTTP failure, back off 2s, 4s, 8s, then 15s.
- Poll URL: /api/pair?code=<key>&b=<GLASSTUBE_BUILD>&i=<instanceId>&who=<hud|preview>. instanceId is a random 6-character id per page load. who is 'preview' when hasNativeHook() or the user agent matches iPhone or iPad.
- Watchdog: setInterval every 10s. If no poll has started for 30s while visible, restart the chain.
- startPairPoll() guards on pairKey(), not pairCode. Today it never starts when only the link token exists.
- Reset pairLastSeq to -1 whenever pairKey() changes, inside linkStore() and pairCodeStore().
- Keep the destSeq !== pairLastSeq test, not >. Single-flight already prevents out-of-order responses, and > would block every push after a server-side seq reset. This resolves the perf audit's 'monotonic >' against the reliability audit's seq-reset concern.

4. 'Gone' guard:
- pollPair counts dead responses: { ok: false } with /expir|not active|not found|unknown/ or d.gone === true.
- Wipe the link and re-mint only after 3 dead responses at least 30s apart in total. Reset the count on any ok response.
- While strikes are counting, pair-help says 'Checking your link…'.

5. Self-update:
- On every successful poll: if d.build && d.build !== window.GLASSTUBE_BUILD, set updatePending = d.build and send hudNote('update-pending', { from, to }) once.
- maybeUpdate() runs after each poll and from a 5s idle check. It reloads only when all of these hold: updatePending is set; not hidden; current === 'home'; Date.now() - lastKeyAt >= 20000; no push applied in the last 60s; the URL's rv is not already updatePending; and localStorage 'glasstube.reloadedFor' is not { build: updatePending } from less than 10 minutes ago.
- Resume path, on visibilitychange to visible or on pageshow: if updatePending and current is not 'player' and no search text is typed, call show('home') and reload immediately. This is the 'I reopened the app' moment, before any input.
- reloadForUpdate():
  - Call progressSave().
  - Set sessionStorage 'glasstube.updatedFrom' = GLASSTUBE_BUILD.
  - Set localStorage 'glasstube.reloadedFor' = { build, at }.
  - Build u = new URL(location.href), call u.searchParams.set('rv', build), which keeps any ?pair=, then call location.replace(u).
- If a push arrives while an update is pending, play it on the current code. The reload waits for the next safe moment.
- After load: if sessionStorage has updatedFrom, show the toast 'Updated · v<build>' for 2.5s, send hudNote('updated', { from, to }), and clear the marker.

6. Lifecycle handlers:
- visibilitychange: when visible, set lastActiveAt, call pollNow() and run the resume path. When hidden, reschedule at the hidden cadence.
- pageshow (including persisted): same as visible.
- window 'focus' and 'online': pollNow().

7. Launch stamp:
- Add <span id=build-chip> to the home header with 'v<build>', 22px in --t3 (tokens arrive in WP2; use #aaafb9 until then). Fade it to opacity 0 at 3s.
- Splash: remove the dead .splash-icon code. Call hideSplash() 300ms after boot. Change the fade in styles.css .splash to 200ms.

8. Launch path:
- Delete the Player.preload() call (app.js:1874) so YouTube iframe_api never loads in the HUD.
- Remove <link rel=preload href=/icon-192.png> from index.html.

9. From iPhone stop-gap:
- In index.html, put #btn-phone-back first in the screen's DOM order so it gets default focus.
- Rename #btn-pair-new to 'Link a different phone' and require two pinches. The first pinch sets the label 'Pinch again to unlink your iPhone' and arms for 4000ms, then the label reverts. Only a second pinch inside that window runs today's unlink code, plus hudNote('unlink').

10. Diagnostics (debugLines):
- New first rows: Build, Server build, Update ('none', 'waiting for idle home' or 'reloaded from <x>'), Last poll ('3s ago · ok' or the error), Poll every (s), Instance.
- Add the row 'Old version? Middle-finger tap on the home screen, then Restart.'

11. Tooling, in the scratchpad and not the repo: in shot.mjs and audit/player/shotp.mjs, answer POST /api/diag like POST /api/watch (print it as [hud-report], do not forward it). Audit runs then stop polluting production logs.

1. Input arbiter. Replace the bare keydown listener (app.js:1741) with one capture-phase arbiter.
- resolveKey(e): try e.key, then e.code, then keyCode 37-40 and 13, then Android keycodes 19-22, 23 and 66. Escape, Backspace, BrowserBack and GoBack map to 'back'. A single printable character maps to { char }. Anything else returns null and the event is ignored, never guessed.
- Constants in one INPUT object:
  - DUP_MS = 120: the same key within 120ms is one gesture. The harness spaces keys 140ms apart.
  - ENTER_LOCK_MS = 320: ignore Enter for 320ms after any arrow.

- preventDefault() on every handled key. Record lastKeyAt and lastActiveAt.
- Count dropped duplicates and locked Enters for Diagnostics.

2. Navigation stack:
- navStack holds entries { name, render, focusKey, scrollTop }. Home is depth 0.
- At boot: history.replaceState({ gt: 1, d: 0 }, '').
- navTo(entry) saves the current focusKey (data-key on rows: video id, data-menu or channel id) and scrollTop. It then calls history.pushState({ gt: 1, d: depth }) while depth <= 4, otherwise replaceState, and renders.
- goBack(), used by ArrowLeft and back keys: if depth > 0 and history.state.d === depth, call history.back(). Otherwise pop internally and call replaceState.
- The popstate handler pops navStack down to e.state.d (0 when e.state is null), re-renders the top entry from cached data, and restores focus by focusKey, then index, then the first video row. It never calls pushState.
- Channel pages ('More channels') replace the current entry instead of pushing.
- Opening the player from a list is a navTo. Next, previous and retry inside the player are not.
- A phone push does navTo(the 'From iPhone' or playlist queue list), then navTo(player). Back then lands on the queue with the played row focused, replacing goBack's special case that sent 'From iPhone' straight to Home.
- reloadForUpdate (from WP1) now requires depth 0. On resume with depth > 0 and not in the player, call history.go(-depth) and reload on the resulting root popstate.

- navGen++ on every navTo, goBack and popstate.

workPackages.goal: Searching costs a pinch and a sentence when the composer exists, or about 12-17 band inputs instead of 33-59 when it does not. Every visible search control is reachable with the band.
workPackages.changes:
1. Native search field (index.html):
- Replace #kb-text with <input id=kb-input type=search enterkeyhint=search autocomplete=off placeholder='Pinch to speak or type'>, styled as the design system's 52px field.
- It is row -2 of the cursor model, reached with Up from the chips or the top grid row.
- When the cursor lands on it, give it DOM focus. A pinch then opens the system composer on firmware v127 or later.
- Read the text from 'input' and 'change' into typed, uppercased. Strip ' " _ [ ].
- Enter or 'change' with text runs runSearch(). Down from the input calls blur() and moves to the chips or the grid.
- While the input has focus, the WP3 arbiter still handles Up, Down and Enter but lets printable characters through.
- Keep the field showing the end of the query: input.scrollLeft = input.scrollWidth after each change.

2. Chips row (row -1), class kb-chip, cursor class kb-on:
- Show the 4 most recent queries.
- Once typed has 2 or more letters, replace them with up to 4 suggestions, debounced 300ms, from GET /api/suggest?q=. Run the request through the WP3 navGen guard and give it a 3s AbortController timeout. On failure, fall back to recents silently.
- Left and Right move along the row; a pinch sets typed to the chip and runs it.
- Up from grid row 0 enters the chips, or the input if there are none. Re-running a recent search costs a pinch, Up, pinch.

- Keep the 10x4 layout. The nav audit's calculation showed re-ordering does not pay.
- Keep horizontal wrap; remove vertical wrap.

HUD asking the phone for a fresh file when a queued video has none or it expires soon (the phone only attaches files to the first 8 videos): deferred. It needs a new listener in the iPhone app (WebScreen.swift). WP5 at least reuses still-valid files kept in memory.
Relay page (MediaRelay.swift) can strand the glasses on the phone's HTTP page: deferred, iPhone code. WP7 makes the relay reachable but keeps it an explicit choice.
Account sync adopting a dead pairing on a reinstalled phone (Store.swift): deferred, iPhone code. WP6 marks replaced pairings, so the phone unpairs itself on its next check anyway.

Detailed delivery messages in the iPhone app (reading delivery and glassesSeenS, a 'Type on iPhone' search push, a QR install link with ?pair=): deferred, iPhone code. WP6 already makes the phone's existing banner honest through ok and error text, and returns the new fields for a later app build.

Service worker or offline shell: deferred. A cached page would add a stale-build failure on top of the stale-build problem WP1 solves. The no-store page plus self-update is enough. Revisit only with a ?swreset=1 escape hatch.
Long-press and double-pinch gestures: deferred until the WP3 Input test measures the real band. Double-pinch would also delay every single pinch by about 300ms.
Asking the phone for 360p or lower (itag 18): deferred. The phone chooses the itag, and push.js already accepts only 18 or 22.
Self-hosting Roboto, as the perf audit proposed: rejected in favour of the research's local font stack, which downloads nothing.

Visual audit's 16px text floor, a thumbnail on the Continue row, and a permanent thin progress line during playback: rejected. Meta's 18px floor wins, Home has to fit one screen, and a lens showing only the video is cleaner and uses less battery.
Meta's 475ms/625ms focus animation: replaced by 180ms/240ms on opacity only, because swipes arrive under 140ms apart and content updates at 30 Hz.
The README's 'Up goes to the previous video in the first 5s': dropped. Previous moves into the player menu so Up always rewinds.
'More results' paging after 20 search results: deferred. It needs continuation support in feed.js and matters less than dictation and suggestions.
Moving the link token from the poll URL into a header: deferred. Low urgency, since Vercel keeps about 1h of logs; do it in a later server pass.
Server-chosen poll interval (nextPollMs): deferred. The cadence rules in WP1 cut idle traffic by about 60-70%; add it only if Vercel quota becomes a problem.
